import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Ring.Finset
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Choose.Sum
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Field
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.Positivity
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring
import Mathlib.Tactic.NormNum
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp

open Finset

/-! # Lake inventory (SYNTHETIC survey VCS-LK-001) — review packet

SUPPLIED INFORMATION (data): per species camera labels y (all 18 videos), reference-video
calibration (hits/160, false labels/200), eDNA positive grabs k of 18 (any of 3 PCR libs),
blanks (1 positive of 16 field-blank taxon x grab cells), footprint 1260 m2 per pass of 57782.56 m2
mapped area, 2 passes.  See `mkSp` / `lakeSpecies`.

MODELLING CHOICES (not inferred; for review): (1) N=0 iff absent; prior P(N>0)=omega (table in
`lakeSpecies`, judgement, NOT from these data); N|present ~ 1/n on 1..100000 (scale-invariant,
capped). (2) camera labels = false labels (Binomial(36,phi)) + true encounters (Binomial(2N,q)),
phi, d from calibration by grid Bayes with flat prior; q = coverFrac*tau*d, tau = unidentified
field/reference transfer factor, reported as a scenario. (3) eDNA: grab positives patterned
Bernoulli with rate theta~flat if present, contamination f~grid posterior from blanks if absent.
(4) species independent given tau; non-panel fish excluded; sonar unused; mapped areas exact.
PROVED: normalisation/likelihood laws, presence formula, posterior laws, conv law of total, additive
mean/variance (`lake_answer`).  Numbers are NOT proved in Lean (see report.txt). -/

/-- Binomial pmf: number of successes in `m` independent trials of success probability `p`. -/
def binomPmf (m : ℕ) (p : ℝ) (k : ℕ) : ℝ := (m.choose k : ℝ) * p ^ k * (1 - p) ^ (m - k)

theorem binomPmf_nonneg (m : ℕ) {p : ℝ} (h0 : 0 ≤ p) (h1 : p ≤ 1) (k : ℕ) : 0 ≤ binomPmf m p k := by
  unfold binomPmf
  have : 0 ≤ 1 - p := by linarith
  positivity

theorem binomPmf_sum (m : ℕ) (p : ℝ) : ∑ k ∈ range (m + 1), binomPmf m p k = 1 := by
  have h := add_pow p (1 - p) m
  have h2 : (p + (1 - p)) ^ m = 1 := by simp
  rw [h2] at h
  rw [h]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun k _ => ?_)
  unfold binomPmf; ring

/-- `L` is a probability law on `{0,…,M}` (values beyond `M` are never used). -/
structure IsLaw (M : ℕ) (w : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop where
  nonneg : ∀ n, 0 ≤ w n
  sum_one : ∑ n ∈ range (M + 1), w n = 1

/-- Expectation of `g` under `w` on `{0,…,M}`. -/
def E (M : ℕ) (w : ℕ → ℝ) (g : ℕ → ℝ) : ℝ := ∑ n ∈ range (M + 1), w n * g n
def mean (M : ℕ) (w : ℕ → ℝ) : ℝ := E M w (fun n => (n : ℝ))
def var (M : ℕ) (w : ℕ → ℝ) : ℝ := E M w (fun n => ((n : ℝ) - mean M w) ^ 2)

/-- Law of `X + Y` for independent `X ~ a` on `{0..M1}` and `Y ~ b` on `{0..M2}`. -/
def conv (M1 M2 : ℕ) (a b : ℕ → ℝ) : ℕ → ℝ := fun t =>
  ∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1), if i + j = t then a i * b j else 0

theorem conv_E (M1 M2 : ℕ) (a b : ℕ → ℝ) (g : ℕ → ℝ) :
    E (M1 + M2) (conv M1 M2 a b) g =
      ∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1), a i * b j * g (i + j) := by
  unfold E conv
  simp only [Finset.sum_mul]
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i hi => ?_)
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun j hj => ?_)
  have hm : i + j ∈ range (M1 + M2 + 1) := by
    simp only [Finset.mem_range] at hi hj ⊢; omega
  simp [ite_mul, hm]

theorem conv_isLaw {M1 M2 : ℕ} {a b : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : IsLaw M1 a) (hb : IsLaw M2 b) :
    IsLaw (M1 + M2) (conv M1 M2 a b) := by
  constructor
  · intro t
    unfold conv
    refine Finset.sum_nonneg (fun i _ => Finset.sum_nonneg (fun j _ => ?_))
    split_ifs
    · exact mul_nonneg (ha.nonneg i) (hb.nonneg j)
    · exact le_refl _
  · have h := conv_E M1 M2 a b (fun _ => 1)
    unfold E at h
    simp only [mul_one] at h
    rw [h]
    simp only [← Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_mul]
    rw [hb.sum_one]
    simp [ha.sum_one]

/-- Summing out the second factor of a product law. -/
theorem sum_prod_left {M1 M2 : ℕ} {a b : ℕ → ℝ} (hb : IsLaw M2 b) (F : ℕ → ℝ) :
    ∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1), a i * b j * F i
      = ∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), a i * F i := by
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => ?_)
  have : ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1), a i * b j * F i = (a i * F i) * ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1), b j := by
    rw [Finset.mul_sum]; refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun j _ => ?_); ring
  rw [this, hb.sum_one, mul_one]

theorem sum_prod_right {M1 M2 : ℕ} {a b : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : IsLaw M1 a) (F : ℕ → ℝ) :
    ∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1), a i * b j * F j
      = ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1), b j * F j := by
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  have : ∀ j, ∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), a i * b j * F j = (b j * F j) * ∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), a i := by
    intro j; rw [Finset.mul_sum]; refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => ?_); ring
  simp only [this, ha.sum_one, mul_one]

theorem mean_conv {M1 M2 : ℕ} {a b : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : IsLaw M1 a) (hb : IsLaw M2 b) :
    mean (M1 + M2) (conv M1 M2 a b) = mean M1 a + mean M2 b := by
  unfold mean
  rw [conv_E]
  have h : ∀ i j : ℕ, a i * b j * ((((i + j : ℕ)) : ℝ)) =
      a i * b j * (i : ℝ) + a i * b j * (j : ℝ) := by intro i j; push_cast; ring
  simp only [h, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  rw [sum_prod_left hb (fun i => (i : ℝ)), sum_prod_right ha (fun j => (j : ℝ))]
  rfl

theorem var_conv {M1 M2 : ℕ} {a b : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : IsLaw M1 a) (hb : IsLaw M2 b) :
    var (M1 + M2) (conv M1 M2 a b) = var M1 a + var M2 b := by
  unfold var
  rw [mean_conv ha hb, conv_E]
  set ma := mean M1 a
  set mb := mean M2 b
  have hca : ∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), a i * ((i : ℝ) - ma) = 0 := by
    have : ∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), a i * ((i : ℝ) - ma) = mean M1 a - ma * 1 := by
      simp only [mul_sub, Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
      rw [← ha.sum_one]; simp [mean, E, Finset.mul_sum, mul_comm]
    rw [this]; simp [ma]
  have hcb : ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1), b j * ((j : ℝ) - mb) = 0 := by
    have : ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1), b j * ((j : ℝ) - mb) = mean M2 b - mb * 1 := by
      simp only [mul_sub, Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
      rw [← hb.sum_one]; simp [mean, E, Finset.mul_sum, mul_comm]
    rw [this]; simp [mb]
  have h : ∀ i j : ℕ, a i * b j * ((((i + j : ℕ)) : ℝ) - (ma + mb)) ^ 2 =
      a i * b j * ((i : ℝ) - ma) ^ 2 + a i * b j * ((j : ℝ) - mb) ^ 2
        + 2 * ((a i * ((i : ℝ) - ma)) * (b j * ((j : ℝ) - mb))) := by
    intro i j; push_cast; ring
  simp only [h, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  rw [sum_prod_left hb (fun i => ((i : ℝ) - ma) ^ 2), sum_prod_right ha (fun j => ((j : ℝ) - mb) ^ 2)]
  have hx : ∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1),
      2 * ((a i * ((i : ℝ) - ma)) * (b j * ((j : ℝ) - mb))) = 0 := by
    have : ∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1),
        2 * ((a i * ((i : ℝ) - ma)) * (b j * ((j : ℝ) - mb)))
        = 2 * ((∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), a i * ((i : ℝ) - ma)) *
            (∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1), b j * ((j : ℝ) - mb))) := by
      rw [Finset.sum_mul_sum, Finset.mul_sum]
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => ?_)
      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
    rw [this, hca]; simp
  rw [hx]
  simp [var, E, ma, mb]

/-! ### Parameter grids (finite discretisation of nuisance parameters) -/

/-- Discrete prior/posterior over a probability-valued nuisance parameter: weights `w i`, values `x i`, `i < K`. -/
structure Grid where
  K : ℕ
  w : ℕ → ℝ
  x : ℕ → ℝ

/-- Expectation of `f(parameter)` over the grid. -/
def gridAvg (g : Grid) (f : ℝ → ℝ) : ℝ := ∑ i ∈ range g.K, g.w i * f (g.x i)

/-- Probability weights, parameters in the closed unit interval. -/
structure GridOk (g : Grid) : Prop where
  w_nonneg : ∀ i, i < g.K → 0 ≤ g.w i
  w_sum : ∑ i ∈ range g.K, g.w i = 1
  x_mem : ∀ i, i < g.K → 0 ≤ g.x i ∧ g.x i ≤ 1

/-- Strictly positive weights and parameters strictly inside (0,1); at least one grid point. -/
structure GridPos (g : Grid) : Prop where
  K_pos : 0 < g.K
  w_pos : ∀ i, i < g.K → 0 < g.w i
  x_in : ∀ i, i < g.K → 0 < g.x i ∧ g.x i < 1

theorem gridAvg_nonneg (g : Grid) (hw : ∀ i, i < g.K → 0 ≤ g.w i) {f : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hf : ∀ i, i < g.K → 0 ≤ f (g.x i)) : 0 ≤ (gridAvg g) f :=
  Finset.sum_nonneg (fun i hi => mul_nonneg (hw i (Finset.mem_range.mp hi)) (hf i (Finset.mem_range.mp hi)))

theorem gridAvg_pos (g : Grid) (hp : (GridPos g)) {f : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hf : ∀ i, i < g.K → 0 < f (g.x i)) : 0 < (gridAvg g) f :=
  Finset.sum_pos (fun i hi => mul_pos (hp.w_pos i (Finset.mem_range.mp hi)) (hf i (Finset.mem_range.mp hi)))
    ⟨0, Finset.mem_range.mpr hp.K_pos⟩

/-- A mixture of laws indexed by a grid is a law. -/
theorem mix_isLaw {g : Grid} (hg : (GridOk g)) {M : ℕ} {L : ℝ → ℕ → ℝ}
    (hL : ∀ i, i < g.K → IsLaw M (L (g.x i))) : IsLaw M (fun k => (gridAvg g) (fun p => L p k)) := by
  constructor
  · intro k
    exact (gridAvg_nonneg g) hg.w_nonneg (fun i hi => (hL i hi).nonneg k)
  · unfold gridAvg
    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
    have : ∀ i ∈ range g.K, ∑ k ∈ range (M + 1), g.w i * L (g.x i) k = g.w i := by
      intro i hi
      rw [← Finset.mul_sum, (hL i (Finset.mem_range.mp hi)).sum_one, mul_one]
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl this]
    exact hg.w_sum

theorem binomPmf_isLaw (m : ℕ) {p : ℝ} (h0 : 0 ≤ p) (h1 : p ≤ 1) : IsLaw m (binomPmf m p) :=
  ⟨binomPmf_nonneg m h0 h1, binomPmf_sum m p⟩

theorem binomPmf_pos (m : ℕ) {p : ℝ} (h0 : 0 < p) (h1 : p < 1) {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ m) :
    0 < binomPmf m p k := by
  unfold binomPmf
  have : 0 < 1 - p := by linarith
  have := Nat.choose_pos hk
  positivity

/-- Calibration step: grid posterior of a success probability after `hits` successes in `trials`
trials, from a flat prior on the midpoints `(i+1/2)/K` (Bayes' rule on a grid). -/
noncomputable def calGrid (K hits trials : ℕ) : Grid where
  K := K
  w := fun i => (((i : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / K) ^ hits * (1 - ((i : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / K) ^ (trials - hits) /
    ∑ j ∈ range K, (((j : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / K) ^ hits * (1 - ((j : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / K) ^ (trials - hits)
  x := fun i => ((i : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / K

/-- Flat grid (no calibration information). -/
noncomputable def flatGrid (K : ℕ) : Grid where
  K := K
  w := fun _ => 1 / K
  x := fun i => ((i : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / K

theorem grid_x_in (K : ℕ) {i : ℕ} (hi : i < K) :
    0 < ((i : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / K ∧ ((i : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / K < 1 := by
  have hK : (0 : ℝ) < K := by exact_mod_cast (Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.zero_le _) hi)
  have hi' : (i : ℝ) + 1 ≤ K := by exact_mod_cast hi
  constructor
  · positivity
  · rw [div_lt_one hK]; linarith

theorem grid_x_in' (K : ℕ) (i : ℕ) : 0 ≤ ((i : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / K ∧
    (i < K → ((i : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / K ≤ 1) := by
  refine ⟨by positivity, fun hi => (grid_x_in K hi).2.le⟩

theorem calGrid_pos (K hits trials : ℕ) (hK : 0 < K) : (GridPos (calGrid K hits trials)) := by
  have hterm : ∀ j, j < K → 0 < (((j : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / K) ^ hits *
      (1 - ((j : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / K) ^ (trials - hits) := by
    intro j hj
    have h := grid_x_in K hj
    have : 0 < 1 - ((j : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / K := by linarith [h.2]
    have := h.1
    positivity
  have hS : 0 < ∑ j ∈ range K, (((j : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / K) ^ hits *
      (1 - ((j : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / K) ^ (trials - hits) :=
    Finset.sum_pos (fun j hj => hterm j (Finset.mem_range.mp hj)) ⟨0, Finset.mem_range.mpr hK⟩
  refine ⟨hK, fun i hi => ?_, fun i hi => grid_x_in K hi⟩
  exact div_pos (hterm i hi) hS

theorem flatGrid_pos (K : ℕ) (hK : 0 < K) : (GridPos (flatGrid K)) := by
  refine ⟨hK, fun i _ => ?_, fun i hi => grid_x_in K hi⟩
  have : (0 : ℝ) < K := by exact_mod_cast hK
  show 0 < 1 / (K : ℝ)
  positivity

theorem calGrid_sum (K hits trials : ℕ) (hK : 0 < K) :
    ∑ i ∈ range (calGrid K hits trials).K, (calGrid K hits trials).w i = 1 := by
  have hp := calGrid_pos K hits trials hK
  show ∑ i ∈ range K, _ = 1
  have hS : 0 < ∑ j ∈ range K, (((j : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / K) ^ hits *
      (1 - ((j : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / K) ^ (trials - hits) := by
    refine Finset.sum_pos (fun j hj => ?_) ⟨0, Finset.mem_range.mpr hK⟩
    have h := grid_x_in K (Finset.mem_range.mp hj)
    have : 0 < 1 - ((j : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / K := by linarith [h.2]
    have := h.1
    positivity
  show ∑ i ∈ range K, (_ / _) = 1
  rw [← Finset.sum_div]
  exact div_self hS.ne'

theorem calGrid_ok (K hits trials : ℕ) (hK : 0 < K) : (GridOk (calGrid K hits trials)) := by
  have hp := calGrid_pos K hits trials hK
  exact ⟨fun i hi => (hp.w_pos i hi).le, calGrid_sum K hits trials hK,
    fun i hi => ⟨(hp.x_in i hi).1.le, (hp.x_in i hi).2.le⟩⟩

theorem flatGrid_ok (K : ℕ) (hK : 0 < K) : (GridOk (flatGrid K)) := by
  have hp := flatGrid_pos K hK
  refine ⟨fun i hi => (hp.w_pos i hi).le, ?_, fun i hi => ⟨(hp.x_in i hi).1.le, (hp.x_in i hi).2.le⟩⟩
  show ∑ i ∈ range K, (1 / (K : ℝ)) = 1
  have : (K : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hK.ne'
  simp [this]

/-! ### Species model -/

/-- Harmonic normaliser of the scale-invariant (1/n) prior on `{1,…,M}`. -/
noncomputable def harm (M : ℕ) : ℝ := ∑ k ∈ range M, 1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1)

/-- Everything specific to one species: prior, camera model, eDNA model, observed data. -/
structure Sp where
  M : ℕ        -- carrying-capacity cap on the number of individuals
  omega : ℝ    -- prior probability that the species is present (N > 0)
  y : ℕ        -- observed camera labels of this species (all 18 videos, both size bins)
  m : ℕ        -- number of fish-free-video-like opportunities for a false label (18 videos x 2 bins)
  c : ℕ        -- number of independent passes (each fish can be encountered once per pass)
  gF : Grid    -- per-opportunity false-label probability
  gQ : Grid    -- per-fish, per-pass probability of a correctly labelled encounter
  k : ℕ        -- water grabs with species-positive eDNA
  nG : ℕ       -- total water grabs
  gC : Grid    -- per-grab false-positive (contamination) probability when absent
  gT : Grid    -- per-grab detection probability when present

/-- Prior law of `N`: `P(N=0)=1-ω`; given presence `P(N=n) ∝ 1/n` on `1..M`. -/
noncomputable def spPrior (s : Sp) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  if n = 0 then 1 - s.omega else s.omega * (1 / (n : ℝ)) / harm s.M

/-- Law of the number of false labels. -/
def spPF (s : Sp) : ℕ → ℝ := fun f => (gridAvg s.gF) (fun p => binomPmf s.m p f)
/-- Law of the number of true encounters given `N = n`. -/
def spPT (s : Sp) (n : ℕ) : ℕ → ℝ := fun t => (gridAvg s.gQ) (fun q => binomPmf (s.c * n) q t)
/-- Likelihood of observing `y` camera labels given `N = n`: false labels + true encounters. -/
def spCamLik (s : Sp) (n y : ℕ) : ℝ := conv s.m (s.c * n) (spPF s) ((spPT s) n) y

/-- Probability of the observed eDNA grab pattern given absent / present. -/
def pattern (k nG : ℕ) (p : ℝ) : ℝ := p ^ k * (1 - p) ^ (nG - k)
noncomputable def spEdnaLik (s : Sp) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  if n = 0 then (gridAvg s.gC) (pattern s.k s.nG) else (gridAvg s.gT) (pattern s.k s.nG)

/-- Unnormalised posterior and evidence. -/
noncomputable def spUnnorm (s : Sp) (n : ℕ) : ℝ := (spPrior s) n * (spCamLik s) n s.y * (spEdnaLik s) n
noncomputable def spZ (s : Sp) : ℝ := ∑ n ∈ range (s.M + 1), (spUnnorm s) n
/-- Posterior law of the number of individuals (Bayes' rule). -/
noncomputable def spPost (s : Sp) (n : ℕ) : ℝ := (spUnnorm s) n / (spZ s)

/-- Presence means at least one living individual. -/
noncomputable def spPresence (s : Sp) : ℝ := ∑ n ∈ range (s.M + 1), if 0 < n then (spPost s) n else 0

structure SpValid (s : Sp) : Prop where
  M_pos : 1 ≤ s.M
  omega_pos : 0 < s.omega
  omega_lt : s.omega < 1
  gF : (GridPos s.gF)
  gQ : (GridPos s.gQ)
  gC : (GridPos s.gC)
  gT : (GridPos s.gT)
  gFo : (GridOk s.gF)
  gQo : (GridOk s.gQ)
  gCo : (GridOk s.gC)
  gTo : (GridOk s.gT)
  y_le : s.y ≤ s.c * s.M
  nG_ge : s.k ≤ s.nG

theorem harm_pos {M : ℕ} (h : 1 ≤ M) : 0 < harm M := by
  unfold harm
  refine Finset.sum_pos (fun k _ => by positivity) ⟨0, Finset.mem_range.mpr h⟩

theorem prior_isLaw {s : Sp} (h : (SpValid s)) : IsLaw s.M (spPrior s) := by
  have hH := harm_pos h.M_pos
  constructor
  · intro n
    unfold spPrior
    split_ifs
    · linarith [h.omega_lt]
    · have := h.omega_pos; positivity
  · rw [Finset.sum_range_succ']
    simp only [spPrior]
    simp only [Nat.succ_ne_zero, if_false, if_true]
    have : ∑ i ∈ range s.M, s.omega * (1 / (((i + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ))) / harm s.M = s.omega := by
      rw [← Finset.sum_div, ← Finset.mul_sum]
      have : ∑ i ∈ range s.M, (1 / (((i + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ))) = harm s.M := by
        unfold harm; push_cast; rfl
      rw [this]; field_simp
    rw [this]; ring

theorem pF_isLaw {s : Sp} (h : (SpValid s)) : IsLaw s.m (spPF s) :=
  mix_isLaw h.gFo (fun i hi => binomPmf_isLaw s.m (h.gFo.x_mem i hi).1 (h.gFo.x_mem i hi).2)

theorem pT_isLaw {s : Sp} (h : (SpValid s)) (n : ℕ) : IsLaw (s.c * n) ((spPT s) n) :=
  mix_isLaw h.gQo (fun i hi => binomPmf_isLaw (s.c * n) (h.gQo.x_mem i hi).1 (h.gQo.x_mem i hi).2)

/-- The camera likelihood is a genuine probability law for the data `y` given `N = n`. -/
theorem camLik_isLaw {s : Sp} (h : (SpValid s)) (n : ℕ) :
    IsLaw (s.m + s.c * n) (fun y => (spCamLik s) n y) :=
  conv_isLaw (pF_isLaw h) (pT_isLaw h n)

theorem ednaLik_nonneg {s : Sp} (h : (SpValid s)) (n : ℕ) : 0 ≤ (spEdnaLik s) n := by
  unfold spEdnaLik
  have key : ∀ g : Grid, (GridOk g) → 0 ≤ (gridAvg g) (pattern s.k s.nG) := by
    intro g hg
    refine (gridAvg_nonneg g) hg.w_nonneg (fun i hi => ?_)
    have := hg.x_mem i hi
    unfold pattern
    have : 0 ≤ 1 - g.x i := by linarith [this.2]
    have := (hg.x_mem i hi).1
    positivity
  split_ifs
  · exact key _ h.gCo
  · exact key _ h.gTo

theorem ednaLik_pos {s : Sp} (h : (SpValid s)) (n : ℕ) : 0 < (spEdnaLik s) n := by
  unfold spEdnaLik
  have key : ∀ g : Grid, (GridPos g) → 0 < (gridAvg g) (pattern s.k s.nG) := by
    intro g hg
    refine (gridAvg_pos g) hg (fun i hi => ?_)
    have := hg.x_in i hi
    unfold pattern
    have : 0 < 1 - g.x i := by linarith [this.2]
    have := (hg.x_in i hi).1
    positivity
  split_ifs
  · exact key _ h.gC
  · exact key _ h.gT

theorem unnorm_nonneg {s : Sp} (h : (SpValid s)) (n : ℕ) : 0 ≤ (spUnnorm s) n := by
  unfold spUnnorm
  exact mul_nonneg (mul_nonneg ((prior_isLaw h).nonneg n) ((camLik_isLaw h n).nonneg _))
    (ednaLik_nonneg h n)

theorem conv_pos {M1 M2 : ℕ} {a b : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : ∀ n, 0 ≤ a n) (hb : ∀ n, 0 ≤ b n)
    (ha0 : 0 < a 0) {y : ℕ} (hy : y ≤ M2) (hby : 0 < b y) : 0 < conv M1 M2 a b y := by
  unfold conv
  have h0 : 0 ∈ range (M1 + 1) := Finset.mem_range.mpr (Nat.succ_pos _)
  have hyr : y ∈ range (M2 + 1) := Finset.mem_range.mpr (Nat.lt_succ_of_le hy)
  have inner_nn : ∀ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), 0 ≤ ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1),
      (if i + j = y then a i * b j else 0) := fun i _ =>
    Finset.sum_nonneg (fun j _ => by split_ifs; exact mul_nonneg (ha i) (hb j); exact le_refl _)
  have h1 := Finset.single_le_sum inner_nn h0
  have h2 := Finset.single_le_sum (f := fun j => if 0 + j = y then a 0 * b j else 0)
    (fun j _ => by split_ifs; exact mul_nonneg (ha 0) (hb j); exact le_refl _) hyr
  simp only [zero_add, if_true] at h2
  have : 0 < a 0 * b y := mul_pos ha0 hby
  simp only [zero_add] at h1
  linarith

theorem camLik_pos {s : Sp} (h : (SpValid s)) : 0 < (spCamLik s) s.M s.y := by
  unfold spCamLik
  have hF0 : 0 < (spPF s) 0 := by
    refine (gridAvg_pos s.gF) h.gF (fun i hi => binomPmf_pos s.m (h.gF.x_in i hi).1 (h.gF.x_in i hi).2 (Nat.zero_le _))
  have hT : 0 < (spPT s) s.M s.y :=
    (gridAvg_pos s.gQ) h.gQ (fun i hi => binomPmf_pos _ (h.gQ.x_in i hi).1 (h.gQ.x_in i hi).2 h.y_le)
  exact conv_pos (pF_isLaw h).nonneg (pT_isLaw h s.M).nonneg hF0 h.y_le hT

/-- The data are possible under the model: the evidence is strictly positive. -/
theorem Z_pos {s : Sp} (h : (SpValid s)) : 0 < (spZ s) := by
  unfold spZ
  have hH := harm_pos h.M_pos
  refine Finset.sum_pos' (fun n _ => unnorm_nonneg h n) ⟨s.M, Finset.mem_range.mpr (Nat.lt_succ_self _), ?_⟩
  unfold spUnnorm spPrior
  have hM : s.M ≠ 0 := by have := h.M_pos; omega
  simp only [hM, if_false]
  have := h.omega_pos
  have hMr : (0 : ℝ) < s.M := by exact_mod_cast Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hM
  have := camLik_pos h
  have := ednaLik_pos h s.M
  positivity

/-- The posterior is a probability law on `{0,…,M}`. -/
theorem post_isLaw {s : Sp} (h : (SpValid s)) : IsLaw s.M (spPost s) := by
  have hZ := Z_pos h
  constructor
  · intro n; exact div_nonneg (unnorm_nonneg h n) hZ.le
  · unfold spPost
    rw [← Finset.sum_div]
    exact div_self hZ.ne'

/-- Posterior probability of presence (`N > 0`) is `1 - P(N = 0 | data)`, with the explicit form of
`P(N=0 | data)`. -/
theorem presence_formula {s : Sp} (h : (SpValid s)) :
    (spPresence s) = 1 - (1 - s.omega) * (spCamLik s) 0 s.y * (gridAvg s.gC) (pattern s.k s.nG) / (spZ s) := by
  have hl := (post_isLaw h).sum_one
  unfold spPresence
  rw [Finset.sum_range_succ'] at hl ⊢
  simp only [Nat.succ_pos, if_true, lt_self_iff_false, if_false, add_zero] at hl ⊢
  have h0 : (spPost s) 0 = (1 - s.omega) * (spCamLik s) 0 s.y * (gridAvg s.gC) (pattern s.k s.nG) / (spZ s) := by
    simp [spPost, spUnnorm, spPrior, spEdnaLik]
  linarith

/-- With no camera false labels possible, one labelled encounter excludes absence. -/
theorem camera_excludes_absence {s : Sp} (h : (SpValid s)) (hy : 0 < s.y)
    (hnofp : ∀ i, i < s.gF.K → s.gF.x i = 0) : (spPresence s) = 1 := by
  rw [presence_formula h]
  have hz : (spCamLik s) 0 s.y = 0 := by
    unfold spCamLik conv
    refine Finset.sum_eq_zero (fun i _ => Finset.sum_eq_zero (fun j hjm => ?_))
    have hj : j = 0 := by simp at hjm; omega
    split_ifs with hij
    · have hi : i ≠ 0 := by omega
      have : (spPF s) i = 0 := by
        unfold spPF gridAvg
        refine Finset.sum_eq_zero (fun l hl => ?_)
        rw [hnofp l (Finset.mem_range.mp hl)]
        simp [binomPmf, hi]
      rw [this, zero_mul]
    · rfl
  rw [hz]; simp

/-- Independence: with a product prior and a product likelihood, the joint posterior of two
species is the product of the marginal posteriors. -/
theorem joint_posterior_factorizes {M1 M2 : ℕ} {pa pb la lb : ℕ → ℝ}
    (hZa : ∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), pa i * la i ≠ 0) (hZb : ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1), pb j * lb j ≠ 0)
    (i j : ℕ) :
    (pa i * pb j * (la i * lb j)) /
        ∑ i' ∈ range (M1 + 1), ∑ j' ∈ range (M2 + 1), pa i' * pb j' * (la i' * lb j') =
      ((pa i * la i) / ∑ i' ∈ range (M1 + 1), pa i' * la i') *
        ((pb j * lb j) / ∑ j' ∈ range (M2 + 1), pb j' * lb j') := by
  have : ∑ i' ∈ range (M1 + 1), ∑ j' ∈ range (M2 + 1), pa i' * pb j' * (la i' * lb j') =
      (∑ i' ∈ range (M1 + 1), pa i' * la i') * ∑ j' ∈ range (M2 + 1), pb j' * lb j' := by
    rw [Finset.sum_mul_sum]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i' _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun j' _ => ?_))
    ring
  rw [this]
  field_simp

/-! ### Total population -/

/-- Law (support bound, pmf) of the total of a list of independent species counts. -/
noncomputable def totalLaw : List Sp → ℕ × (ℕ → ℝ)
  | [] => (0, fun n => if n = 0 then 1 else 0)
  | s :: ss => (s.M + (totalLaw ss).1, conv s.M (totalLaw ss).1 (spPost s) (totalLaw ss).2)

theorem totalLaw_spec : ∀ l : List Sp, (∀ s ∈ l, (SpValid s)) →
    IsLaw (totalLaw l).1 (totalLaw l).2 ∧
    mean (totalLaw l).1 (totalLaw l).2 = (l.map (fun s => mean s.M (spPost s))).sum ∧
    var (totalLaw l).1 (totalLaw l).2 = (l.map (fun s => var s.M (spPost s))).sum
  | [], _ => by
    refine ⟨⟨fun n => ?_, ?_⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
    · simp only [totalLaw]; split_ifs <;> norm_num
    · simp [totalLaw]
    · simp [totalLaw, mean, E]
    · simp [totalLaw, var, E, mean]
  | s :: ss, hv => by
    have hs : (SpValid s) := hv s (List.mem_cons_self ..)
    obtain ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩ := totalLaw_spec ss (fun t ht => hv t (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ ht))
    have hl := post_isLaw hs
    refine ⟨conv_isLaw hl h1, ?_, ?_⟩
    · simp only [totalLaw, List.map_cons, List.sum_cons]
      rw [mean_conv hl h1, h2]
    · simp only [totalLaw, List.map_cons, List.sum_cons]
      rw [var_conv hl h1, h3]

/-- **Answer.** For independent species counts whose posteriors are defined by the Bayesian model
above: each species posterior is a probability law, its presence probability is given by the
explicit formula, a labelled camera encounter excludes absence when no false labels are possible,
and the total population posterior is the convolution of the species laws, a probability law
whose mean and variance are the sums of the species means and variances. -/
theorem answer_theorem : ∀ l : List Sp, (∀ s ∈ l, (SpValid s)) →
    (∀ s ∈ l, IsLaw s.M (spPost s) ∧
      (spPresence s) = 1 - (1 - s.omega) * (spCamLik s) 0 s.y * (gridAvg s.gC) (pattern s.k s.nG) / (spZ s)) ∧
    IsLaw (totalLaw l).1 (totalLaw l).2 ∧
    mean (totalLaw l).1 (totalLaw l).2 = (l.map (fun s => mean s.M (spPost s))).sum ∧
    var (totalLaw l).1 (totalLaw l).2 = (l.map (fun s => var s.M (spPost s))).sum := by
  intro l hv
  exact ⟨fun s hs => ⟨post_isLaw (hv s hs), presence_formula (hv s hs)⟩, totalLaw_spec l hv⟩

/-! ### The lake: data and explicit modelling choices -/

/-- Rescale the parameters of a grid by a factor `a` (used for transfer/coverage). -/
def scaledGrid (g : Grid) (a : ℝ) : Grid where
  K := g.K
  w := g.w
  x := fun i => a * g.x i

theorem scaledGrid_pos {g : Grid} (hg : (GridPos g)) {a : ℝ} (h0 : 0 < a) (h1 : a ≤ 1) :
    (GridPos (scaledGrid g a)) := by
  refine ⟨hg.K_pos, hg.w_pos, fun i hi => ?_⟩
  have := hg.x_in i hi
  show 0 < a * g.x i ∧ a * g.x i < 1
  constructor
  · exact mul_pos h0 this.1
  · nlinarith [this.1, this.2]

theorem scaledGrid_ok {g : Grid} (hg : (GridOk g)) {a : ℝ} (h0 : 0 ≤ a) (h1 : a ≤ 1) :
    (GridOk (scaledGrid g a)) := by
  refine ⟨hg.w_nonneg, hg.w_sum, fun i hi => ?_⟩
  have := hg.x_mem i hi
  show 0 ≤ a * g.x i ∧ a * g.x i ≤ 1
  constructor
  · exact mul_nonneg h0 this.1
  · nlinarith [this.1, this.2]

/-- Fraction of the mapped lake area (57 782.56 m²) covered by the 9 camera footprints (1260 m²)
of one pass. -/
noncomputable def coverFrac : ℝ := 1260 / 57782.56

theorem coverFrac_bounds : 0 < coverFrac ∧ coverFrac < 1 := by
  unfold coverFrac; constructor <;> norm_num

/-- One panel species.  `om` prior presence probability; `y` camera labels; `calHits` correct
labels out of 160 reference encounters; `fpHits` false labels in 200 fish-free reference videos;
`k` eDNA-positive grabs of 18; `tau` field/reference detectability transfer factor. -/
noncomputable def mkSp (om : ℝ) (y calHits fpHits k : ℕ) (tau : ℝ) : Sp where
  M := 100000
  omega := om
  y := y
  m := 36
  c := 2
  gF := calGrid 20 fpHits 200
  gQ := scaledGrid (calGrid 20 calHits 160) (coverFrac * tau)
  k := k
  nG := 18
  gC := calGrid 20 1 16
  gT := flatGrid 20

/-- The eight panel species, in order: perch, roach, ruffe, pike, burbot, bleak, vendace, bream. -/
noncomputable def lakeSpecies (tau : ℝ) : List Sp :=
  [ mkSp (97 / 100) 39 97 2 17 tau, mkSp (9 / 10) 26 82 2 17 tau,
    mkSp (8 / 10) 1 29 1 14 tau, mkSp (9 / 10) 1 67 6 9 tau,
    mkSp (6 / 10) 1 24 4 1 tau, mkSp (35 / 100) 0 92 1 1 tau,
    mkSp (3 / 10) 0 78 3 0 tau, mkSp (35 / 100) 1 75 2 1 tau ]

theorem mkSp_valid {om : ℝ} (h0 : 0 < om) (h1 : om < 1) {y : ℕ} (hy : y ≤ 200000)
    (calHits fpHits : ℕ) {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ 18) {tau : ℝ} (t0 : 0 < tau) (t1 : tau ≤ 1) :
    (SpValid (mkSp om y calHits fpHits k tau)) := by
  have hc := coverFrac_bounds
  have ha0 : 0 < coverFrac * tau := mul_pos hc.1 t0
  have ha1 : coverFrac * tau ≤ 1 := by nlinarith [hc.2]
  have k20 : 0 < 20 := by norm_num
  have kk : 0 < 16 := by norm_num
  have hM : 1 ≤ (100000 : ℕ) := by norm_num
  have hy' : y ≤ 2 * 100000 := by omega
  exact ⟨hM, h0, h1,
    calGrid_pos 20 _ _ k20, scaledGrid_pos (calGrid_pos 20 _ _ k20) ha0 ha1,
    calGrid_pos 20 _ _ k20, flatGrid_pos 20 k20,
    calGrid_ok 20 _ _ k20, scaledGrid_ok (calGrid_ok 20 _ _ k20) ha0.le ha1,
    calGrid_ok 20 _ _ k20, flatGrid_ok 20 k20,
    hy', hk⟩

theorem lake_valid {tau : ℝ} (t0 : 0 < tau) (t1 : tau ≤ 1) : ∀ s ∈ lakeSpecies tau, (SpValid s) := by
  intro s hs
  simp only [lakeSpecies, List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil, or_false] at hs
  rcases hs with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    exact mkSp_valid (by norm_num) (by norm_num) (by norm_num) _ _ (by norm_num) t0 t1

/-- **Conclusion for the lake.**  For every field/reference detectability transfer factor
`tau ∈ (0,1]`: each panel species' posterior count law is a probability law on `{0..100000}` with
presence probability `1 - P(N=0 | data)` given by the explicit formula, and the posterior law of
the total panel-species count (independent species) is a probability law whose mean and variance
are the sums of the eight species posterior means and variances. -/
theorem lake_answer : ∀ tau : ℝ, 0 < tau → tau ≤ 1 →
    (∀ s ∈ lakeSpecies tau, IsLaw s.M (spPost s) ∧
      (spPresence s) = 1 - (1 - s.omega) * (spCamLik s) 0 s.y * (gridAvg s.gC) (pattern s.k s.nG) / (spZ s)) ∧
    IsLaw (totalLaw (lakeSpecies tau)).1 (totalLaw (lakeSpecies tau)).2 ∧
    mean (totalLaw (lakeSpecies tau)).1 (totalLaw (lakeSpecies tau)).2
      = ((lakeSpecies tau).map (fun s => mean s.M (spPost s))).sum ∧
    var (totalLaw (lakeSpecies tau)).1 (totalLaw (lakeSpecies tau)).2
      = ((lakeSpecies tau).map (fun s => var s.M (spPost s))).sum :=
  fun _ t0 t1 => answer_theorem _ (lake_valid t0 t1)

ring\n\n/-- `L` is a probability law on `{0,…,M}` (values beyond `M` are never used). -/\nstructure IsLaw (M : ℕ) (w : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop where\n  nonneg : ∀ n, 0 ≤ w n\n  sum_one : ∑ n ∈ range (M + 1), w n = 1\n\n/-- Expectation of `g` under `w` on `{0,…,M}`. -/\ndef E (M : ℕ) (w : ℕ → ℝ) (g : ℕ → ℝ) : ℝ := ∑ n ∈ range (M + 1), w n * g n\ndef mean (M : ℕ) (w : ℕ → ℝ) : ℝ := E M w (fun n => (n : ℝ))\ndef var (M : ℕ) (w : ℕ → ℝ) : ℝ := E M w (fun n => ((n : ℝ) - mean M w) ^ 2)\n\n/-- Law of `X + Y` for independent `X ~ a` on `{0..M1}` and `Y ~ b` on `{0..M2}`. -/\ndef conv (M1 M2 : ℕ) (a b : ℕ → ℝ) : ℕ → ℝ := fun t =>\n  ∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1), if i + j = t then a i * b j else 0\n\ntheorem conv_E (M1 M2 : ℕ) (a b : ℕ → ℝ) (g : ℕ → ℝ) :\n    E (M1 + M2) (conv M1 M2 a b) g =\n      ∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1), a i * b j * g (i + j) := by\n  unfold E conv\n  simp only [Finset.sum_mul]\n  rw [Finset.sum_comm]\n  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i hi => ?_)\n  rw [Finset.sum_comm]\n  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun j hj => ?_)\n  have hm : i + j ∈ range (M1 + M2 + 1) := by\n    simp only [Finset.mem_range] at hi hj ⊢; omega\n  simp [ite_mul, hm]\n\ntheorem conv_isLaw {M1 M2 : ℕ} {a b : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : IsLaw M1 a) (hb : IsLaw M2 b) :\n    IsLaw (M1 + M2) (conv M1 M2 a b) := by\n  constructor\n  · intro t\n    unfold conv\n    refine Finset.sum_nonneg (fun i _ => Finset.sum_nonneg (fun j _ => ?_))\n    split_ifs\n    · exact mul_nonneg (ha.nonneg i) (hb.nonneg j)\n    · exact le_refl _\n  · have h := conv_E M1 M2 a b (fun _ => 1)\n    unfold E at h\n    simp only [mul_one] at h\n    rw [h]\n    simp only [← Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_mul]\n    rw [hb.sum_one]\n    simp [ha.sum_one]\n\n/-- Summing out the second factor of a product law. -/\ntheorem sum_prod_left {M1 M2 : ℕ} {a b : ℕ → ℝ} (hb : IsLaw M2 b) (F : ℕ → ℝ) :\n    ∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1), a i * b j * F i\n      = ∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), a i * F i := by\n  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => ?_)\n  have : ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1), a i * b j * F i = (a i * F i) * ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1), b j := by\n    rw [Finset.mul_sum]; refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun j _ => ?_); ring\n  rw [this, hb.sum_one, mul_one]\n\ntheorem sum_prod_right {M1 M2 : ℕ} {a b : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : IsLaw M1 a) (F : ℕ → ℝ) :\n    ∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1), a i * b j * F j\n      = ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1), b j * F j := by\n  rw [Finset.sum_comm]\n  have : ∀ j, ∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), a i * b j * F j = (b j * F j) * ∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), a i := by\n    intro j; rw [Finset.mul_sum]; refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => ?_); ring\n  simp only [this, ha.sum_one, mul_one]\n\ntheorem mean_conv {M1 M2 : ℕ} {a b : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : IsLaw M1 a) (hb : IsLaw M2 b) :\n    mean (M1 + M2) (conv M1 M2 a b) = mean M1 a + mean M2 b := by\n  unfold mean\n  rw [conv_E]\n  have h : ∀ i j : ℕ, a i * b j * ((((i + j : ℕ)) : ℝ)) =\n      a i * b j * (i : ℝ) + a i * b j * (j : ℝ) := by intro i j; simp [mean, E, Finset.mul_sum, mul_comm]\n    rw [this]; simp [ma]\n  have hcb : ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1), b j * ((j : ℝ) - mb) = 0 := by\n    have : ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1), b j * ((j : ℝ) - mb) = mean M2 b - mb * 1 := by\n      simp only [mul_sub, Finset.sum_sub_distrib]\n      rw [← hb.sum_one]; simp [mean, E, Finset.mul_sum, mul_comm]\n    rw [this]; simp [mb]\n  have h : ∀ i j : ℕ, a i * b j * ((((i + j : ℕ)) : ℝ) - (ma + mb)) ^ 2 =\n      a i * b j * ((i : ℝ) - ma) ^ 2 + a i * b j * ((j : ℝ) - mb) ^ 2\n        + 2 * ((a i * ((i : ℝ) - ma)) * (b j * ((j : ℝ) - mb))) := by\n    intro i j; push_cast; ring\n  simp only [h, Finset.sum_add_distrib]\n  rw [sum_prod_left hb (fun i => ((i : ℝ) - ma) ^ 2), sum_prod_right ha (fun j => ((j : ℝ) - mb) ^ 2)]\n  have hx : ∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1),\n      2 * ((a i * ((i : ℝ) - ma)) * (b j * ((j : ℝ) - mb))) = 0 := by\n    have : ∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1),\n        2 * ((a i * ((i : ℝ) - ma)) * (b j * ((j : ℝ) - mb)))\n        = 2 * ((∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), a i * ((i : ℝ) - ma)) *\n            (∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1), b j * ((j : ℝ) - mb))) := by\n      rw [Finset.sum_mul_sum, Finset.mul_sum]\n      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => ?_)\n      rw [Finset.mul_sum]\n    rw [this, hca]; simp\n  rw [hx]\n  simp [var, E, ma, mb]\n\n/-! ### Parameter grids (finite discretisation of nuisance parameters) -/\n\n/-- Discrete prior/posterior over a probability-valued nuisance parameter: weights `w i`, values `x i`, `i < K`. -/\nstructure Grid where\n  K : ℕ\n  w : ℕ → ℝ\n  x : ℕ → ℝ\n\n/-- Expectation of `f(parameter)` over the grid. -/\ndef gridAvg (g : Grid) (f : ℝ → ℝ) : ℝ := ∑ i ∈ range g.K, g.w i * f (g.x i)\n\n/-- Probability weights, parameters in the closed unit interval. -/\nstructure GridOk (g : Grid) : Prop where\n  w_nonneg : ∀ i, i < g.K → 0 ≤ g.w i\n  w_sum : ∑ i ∈ range g.K, g.w i = 1\n  x_mem : ∀ i, i < g.K → 0 ≤ g.x i ∧ g.x i ≤ 1\n\n/-- Strictly positive weights and parameters strictly inside (0,1); at least one grid point. -/\nstructure GridPos (g : Grid) : Prop where\n  K_pos : 0 < g.K\n  w_pos : ∀ i, i < g.K → 0 < g.w i\n  x_in : ∀ i, i < g.K → 0 < g.x i ∧ g.x i < 1\n\ntheorem gridAvg_nonneg (g : Grid) (hw : ∀ i, i < g.K → 0 ≤ g.w i) {f : ℝ → ℝ}\n    (hf : ∀ i, i < g.K → 0 ≤ f (g.x i)) : 0 ≤ (gridAvg g) f :=\n  Finset.sum_nonneg (fun i hi => mul_nonneg (hw i (Finset.mem_range.mp hi)) (hf i (Finset.mem_range.mp hi)))\n\ntheorem gridAvg_pos (g : Grid) (hp : (GridPos g)) {f : ℝ → ℝ}\n    (hf : ∀ i, i < g.K → 0 < f (g.x i)) : 0 < (gridAvg g) f :=\n  Finset.sum_pos (fun i hi => mul_pos (hp.w_pos i (Finset.mem_range.mp hi)) (hf i (Finset.mem_range.mp hi)))\n    ⟨0, Finset.mem_range.mpr hp.K_pos⟩\n\n/-- A mixture of laws indexed by a grid is a law. -/\ntheorem mix_isLaw {g : Grid} (hg : (GridOk g)) {M : ℕ} {L : ℝ → ℕ → ℝ}\n    (hL : ∀ i, i < g.K → IsLaw M (L (g.x i))) : IsLaw M (fun k => (gridAvg g) (fun p => L p k)) := by\n  constructor\n  · intro k\n    exact (gridAvg_nonneg g) hg.w_nonneg (fun i hi => (hL i hi).nonneg k)\n  · unfold gridAvg\n    rw [Finset.sum_comm]\n    have : ∀ i ∈ range g.K, ∑ k ∈ range (M + 1), g.w i * L (g.x i) k = g.w i := by\n      intro i hi\n      rw [← Finset.mul_sum, (hL i (Finset.mem_range.mp hi)).sum_one, mul_one]\n    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl this]\n    exact hg.w_sum\n\ntheorem binomPmf_isLaw (m : ℕ) {p : ℝ} (h0 : 0 ≤ p) (h1 : p ≤ 1) : IsLaw m (binomPmf m p) :=\n  ⟨binomPmf_nonneg m h0 h1, binomPmf_sum m p⟩",

/ 2) / K) ^ hits *\n      (1 - ((j : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / K) ^ (trials - hits) :=\n    Finset.sum_pos (fun j hj => hterm j (Finset.mem_range.mp hj)) ⟨0, Finset.mem_range.mpr hK⟩\n  refine ⟨hK, fun i hi => ?_, fun i hi => grid_x_in K hi⟩\n  exact div_pos (hterm i hi) hS\n\ntheorem flatGrid_pos (K : ℕ) (hK : 0 < K) : (GridPos (flatGrid K)) := by\n  refine ⟨hK, fun i _ => ?_, fun i hi => grid_x_in K hi⟩\n  have : (0 : ℝ) < K := by exact_mod_cast hK\n  show 0 < 1 / (K : ℝ)\n  positivity\n\ntheorem calGrid_sum (K hits trials : ℕ) (hK : 0 < K) :\n    ∑ i ∈ range (calGrid K hits trials).K, (calGrid K hits trials).w i = 1 := by\n  have hp := calGrid_pos K hits trials hK\n  show ∑ i ∈ range K, _ = 1\n  have hS : 0 < ∑ j ∈ range K, (((j : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / K) ^ hits *\n      (1 - ((j : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / K) ^ (trials - hits) := by\n    refine Finset.sum_pos (fun j hj => ?_) ⟨0, Finset.mem_range.mpr hK⟩\n    have h := grid_x_in K (Finset.mem_range.mp hj)\n    have : 0 < 1 - ((j : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / K := by linarith [h.2]\n    have := h.1\n    positivity\n  show ∑ i ∈ range K, (_ / _) = 1\n  rw [← Finset.sum_div]\n  exact div_self hS.ne'\n\ntheorem calGrid_ok (K hits trials : ℕ) (hK : 0 < K) : (GridOk (calGrid K hits trials)) := by\n  have hp := calGrid_pos K hits trials hK\n  exact ⟨fun i hi => (hp.w_pos i hi).le, calGrid_sum K hits trials hK,\n    fun i hi => ⟨(hp.x_in i hi).1.le, (hp.x_in i hi).2.le⟩⟩\n\ntheorem flatGrid_ok (K : ℕ) (hK : 0 < K) : (GridOk (flatGrid K)) := by\n  have hp := flatGrid_pos K hK\n  refine ⟨fun i hi => (hp.w_pos i hi).le, ?_, fun i hi => ⟨(hp.x_in i hi).1.le, (hp.x_in i hi).2.le⟩⟩\n  show ∑ i ∈ range K, (1 / (K : ℝ)) = 1\n  have : (K : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hK.ne'\n  simp [this]\n\n/-! ### Species model -/\n\n/-- Harmonic normaliser of the scale-invariant (1/n) prior on `{1,…,M}`. -/\nnoncomputable def harm (M : ℕ) : ℝ := ∑ k ∈ range M, 1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1)\n\n/-- Everything specific to one species: prior, camera model, eDNA model, observed data. -/\nstructure Sp where\n  M : ℕ        -- carrying-capacity cap on the number of individuals\n  omega : ℝ    -- prior probability that the species is present (N > 0)\n  y : ℕ        -- observed camera labels of this species (all 18 videos, both size bins)\n  m : ℕ        -- number of fish-free-video-like opportunities for a false label (18 videos x 2 bins)\n  c : ℕ        -- number of independent passes (each fish can be encountered once per pass)\n  gF : Grid    -- per-opportunity false-label probability\n  gQ : Grid    -- per-fish, per-pass probability of a correctly labelled encounter\n  k : ℕ        -- water grabs with species-positive eDNA\n  nG : ℕ       -- total water grabs\n  gC : Grid    -- per-grab false-positive (contamination) probability when absent\n  gT : Grid    -- per-grab detection probability when present\n\n/-- Prior law of `N`: `P(N=0)=1-ω`; given presence `P(N=n) ∝ 1/n` on `1..M`. -/\nnoncomputable def spPrior (s : Sp) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=\n  if n = 0 then 1 - s.omega else s.omega * (1 / (n : ℝ)) / harm s.M\n\n/-- Law of the number of false labels. -/\ndef spPF (s : Sp) : ℕ → ℝ := fun f => (gridAvg s.gF) (fun p => binomPmf s.m p f)\n/-- Law of the number of true encounters given `N = n`. -/\ndef spPT (s : Sp) (n : ℕ) : ℕ → ℝ := fun t => (gridAvg s.gQ) (fun q => binomPmf (s.c * n) q t)\n/-- Likelihood of observing `y` camera labels given `N = n`: false labels + true encounters. -/\ndef spCamLik (s : Sp) (n y : ℕ) : ℝ := conv s.m (s.c * n) (spPF s) ((spPT s) n) y\n\n/-- Probability of the observed eDNA grab pattern given absent / present. -/\ndef pattern (k nG : ℕ) (p : ℝ) : ℝ := p ^ k * (1 - p) ^ (nG - k)\nnoncomputable def spEdnaLik (s : Sp) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=\n  if n = 0 then (gridAvg s.gC) (pattern s.k s.nG) else (gridAvg s.gT) (pattern s.k s.nG)\n\n/-- Unnormalised posterior and evidence. -/\nnoncomputable def spUnnorm (s : Sp) (n : ℕ) : ℝ := (spPrior s) n * (spCamLik s) n s.y * (spEdnaLik s) n\nnoncomputable def spZ (s : Sp) : ℝ := ∑ n ∈ range (s.M + 1), (spUnnorm s) n\n/-- Posterior law of the number of individuals (Bayes' rule). -/\nnoncomputable def spPost (s : Sp) (n : ℕ) : ℝ := (spUnnorm s) n / (spZ s)\n\n/-- Presence means at least one living individual. -/\nnoncomputable def spPresence (s : Sp) : ℝ := ∑ n ∈ range (s.M + 1), if 0 < n then (spPost s) n else 0\n\nstructure SpValid (s : Sp) : Prop where\n  M_pos : 1 ≤ s.M\n  omega_pos : 0 < s.omega\n  omega_lt : s.omega < 1\n  gF : (GridPos s.gF)\n  gQ : (GridPos s.gQ)\n  gC : (GridPos s.gC)\n  gT : (GridPos s.gT)\n  gFo : (GridOk s.gF)\n  gQo : (GridOk s.gQ)\n  gCo : (GridOk s.gC)\n  gTo : (GridOk s.gT)\n  y_le : s.y ≤ s.c * s.M\n  nG_ge : s.k ≤ s.nG\n\ntheorem harm_pos {M : ℕ} (h : 1 ≤ M) : 0 < harm M := by\n  unfold harm\n  refine Finset.sum_pos (fun k _ => by positivity) ⟨0, Finset.mem_range.mpr h⟩\n\ntheorem prior_isLaw {s : Sp} (h : (SpValid s)) : IsLaw s.M (spPrior s) := by\n  have hH := harm_pos h.M_pos\n  constructor\n  · intro n\n    unfold spPrior\n    split_ifs\n    · linarith [h.omega_lt]\n    · have := h.omega_pos; positivity\n  · rw [Finset.sum_range_succ']\n    simp only [spPrior]\n    simp only [Nat.succ_ne_zero, if_false, if_true]\n    have : ∑ i ∈ range s.M, s.omega * (1 / (((i + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ))) / harm s.M = s.omega := by\n      rw [← Finset.sum_div, ← Finset.mul_sum]\n      have : ∑ i ∈ range s.M, (1 / (((i + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ))) = harm s.M := by\n        unfold harm; push_cast; rfl\n      rw [this]; field_simp\n    rw [this]; ring\n\ntheorem pF_isLaw {s : Sp} (h : (SpValid s)) : IsLaw s.m (spPF s) :=\n  mix_isLaw h.gFo (fun i hi => binomPmf_isLaw s.m (h.gFo.x_mem i hi).1 (h.gFo.x_mem i hi).2)\n\ntheorem pT_isLaw {s : Sp} (h : (SpValid s)) (n : ℕ) : IsLaw (s.c * n) ((spPT s) n) :=\n  mix_isLaw h.gQo (fun i hi => binomPmf_isLaw (s.c * n) (h.gQo.x_mem i hi).1 (h.gQo.x_mem i hi).2)\n\n/-- The camera likelihood is a genuine probability law for the data `y` given `N = n`. -/\ntheorem camLik_isLaw {s : Sp} (h : (SpValid s)) (n : ℕ) :\n    IsLaw (s.m + s.c * n) (fun y => (spCamLik s) n y) :=\n  conv_isLaw (pF_isLaw h) (pT_isLaw h n)\n\ntheorem ednaLik_nonneg {s : Sp} (h : (SpValid s)) (n : ℕ) : 0 ≤ (spEdnaLik s) n := by\n  unfold spEdnaLik\n  have key : ∀ g : Grid, (GridOk g) → 0 ≤ (gridAvg g) (pattern s.k s.nG) := by\n    intro g hg\n    refine (gridAvg_nonneg g) hg.w_nonneg (fun i hi => ?_)\n    have := hg.x_mem i hi\n    unfold pattern\n    have : 0 ≤ 1 - g.x i := by linarith [this.2]\n    have := (hg.x_mem i hi).1\n    positivity\n  split_ifs\n  · exact key _ h.gCo\n  · exact key _ h.gTo\n\ntheorem ednaLik_pos {s : Sp} (h : (SpValid s)) (n : ℕ) : 0 < (spEdnaLik s) n := by\n  unfold spEdnaLik\n  have key : ∀ g : Grid, (GridPos g) → 0 < (gridAvg g) (pattern s.k s.nG) := by\n    intro g hg\n    refine (gridAvg_pos g) hg (fun i hi => ?_)\n    have := hg.x_in i hi\n    unfold pattern\n    have : 0 < 1 - g.x i := by linarith [this.2]\n    have := (hg.x_in i hi).1\n    positivity\n  split_ifs\n  · exact key _ h.gC\n  · exact key _ h.gT\n\ntheorem unnorm_nonneg {s : Sp} (h : (SpValid s)) (n : ℕ) : 0 ≤ (spUnnorm s) n := by\n  unfold spUnnorm\n  exact mul_nonneg (mul_nonneg ((prior_isLaw h).nonneg n) ((camLik_isLaw h n).nonneg _))\n    (ednaLik_nonneg h n)\n\ntheorem conv_pos {M1 M2 : ℕ} {a b : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : ∀ n, 0 ≤ a n) (hb : ∀ n, 0 ≤ b n)\n    (ha0 : 0 < a 0) {y : ℕ} (hy : y ≤ M2) (hby : 0 < b y) : 0 < conv M1 M2 a b y := by\n  unfold conv\n  have h0 : 0 ∈ range (M1 + 1) := Finset.mem_range.mpr (Nat.succ_pos _)\n  have hyr : y ∈ range (M2 + 1) := Finset.mem_range.mpr (Nat.lt_succ_of_le hy)\n  have inner_nn : ∀ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), 0 ≤ ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1),\n      (if i + j = y then a i * b j else 0) := fun i _ =>\n    Finset.sum_nonneg (fun j _ => by split_ifs; exact mul_nonneg (ha i) (hb j); exact le_refl _)\n  have h1 := Finset.single_le_sum inner_nn h0\n  have h2 := Finset.single_le_sum (f := fun j => if 0 + j = y then a 0 * b j else 0)\n    (fun j _ => by split_ifs; exact mul_nonneg (ha 0) (hb j); exact le_refl _) hyr\n  simp only [zero_add, if_true] at h2\n  have : 0 < a 0 * b y := mul_pos ha0 hby\n  simp only [zero_add] at h1\n binomPmf_pos s.m (h.gF.x_in i hi).1 (h.gF.x_in i hi).2 (Nat.zero_le _))\n  have hT : 0 < (spPT s) s.M s.y :=\n    (gridAvg_pos s.gQ) h.gQ (fun i hi => binomPmf_pos _ (h.gQ.x_in i hi).1 (h.gQ.x_in i hi).2 h.y_le)\n  exact conv_pos (pF_isLaw h).nonneg (pT_isLaw h s.M).nonneg hF0 h.y_le hT\n\n/-- The data are possible under the model: the evidence is strictly positive. -/\ntheorem Z_pos {s : Sp} (h : (SpValid s)) : 0 < (spZ s) := by\n  unfold spZ\n  have hH := harm_pos h.M_pos\n  refine Finset.sum_pos' (fun n _ => unnorm_nonneg h n) ⟨s.M, Finset.mem_range.mpr (Nat.lt_succ_self _), ?_⟩\n  unfold spUnnorm spPrior\n  have hM : s.M ≠ 0 := by have := h.M_pos; omega\n  simp only [hM, if_false]\n  have := h.omega_pos\n  have hMr : (0 : ℝ) < s.M := by exact_mod_cast Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hM\n  have := camLik_pos h\n  have := ednaLik_pos h s.M\n  positivity\n\n/-- The posterior is a probability law on `{0,…,M}`. -/\ntheorem post_isLaw {s : Sp} (h : (SpValid s)) : IsLaw s.M (spPost s) := by\n  have hZ := Z_pos h\n  constructor\n  · intro n; exact div_nonneg (unnorm_nonneg h n) hZ.le\n  · unfold spPost\n    rw [← Finset.sum_div]\n    exact div_self hZ.ne'\n\n/-- Posterior probability of presence (`N > 0`) is `1 - P(N = 0 | data)`, with the explicit form of\n`P(N=0 | data)`. -/\ntheorem presence_formula {s : Sp} (h : (SpValid s)) :\n    (spPresence s) = 1 - (1 - s.omega) * (spCamLik s) 0 s.y * (gridAvg s.gC) (pattern s.k s.nG) / (spZ s) := by\n  have hl := (post_isLaw h).sum_one\n  unfold spPresence\n  rw [Finset.sum_range_succ'] at hl ⊢\n  simp only [Nat.succ_pos, if_true, lt_self_iff_false, if_false, add_zero] at hl ⊢\n  have h0 : (spPost s) 0 = (1 - s.omega) * (spCamLik s) 0 s.y * (gridAvg s.gC) (pattern s.k s.nG) / (spZ s) := by\n    simp [spPost, spUnnorm, spPrior, spEdnaLik]\n  linarith\n\n/-- With no camera false labels possible, one labelled encounter excludes absence. -/\ntheorem camera_excludes_absence {s : Sp} (h : (SpValid s)) (hy : 0 < s.y)\n    (hnofp : ∀ i, i < s.gF.K → s.gF.x i = 0) : (spPresence s) = 1 := by\n  rw [presence_formula h]\n  have hz : (spCamLik s) 0 s.y = 0 := by\n    unfold spCamLik conv\n    refine Finset.sum_eq_zero (fun i _ => Finset.sum_eq_zero (fun j hjm => ?_))\n    have hj : j = 0 := by simp at hjm; omega\n    split_ifs with hij\n    · have hi : i ≠ 0 := by omega\n      have : (spPF s) i = 0 := by\n        unfold spPF gridAvg\n        refine Finset.sum_eq_zero (fun l hl => ?_)\n        rw [hnofp l (Finset.mem_range.mp hl)]\n        simp [binomPmf, hi]\n      rw [this, zero_mul]\n    · rfl\n  rw [hz]; simp\n\n/-- Independence: with a product prior and a product likelihood, the joint posterior of two\nspecies is the product of the marginal posteriors. -/\ntheorem joint_posterior_factorizes {M1 M2 : ℕ} {pa pb la lb : ℕ → ℝ}\n    (hZa : ∑ i ∈ range (M1 + 1), pa i * la i ≠ 0) (hZb : ∑ j ∈ range (M2 + 1), pb j * lb j ≠ 0)\n    (i j : ℕ) :\n    (pa i * pb j * (la i * lb j)) /\n        ∑ i' ∈ range (M1 + 1), ∑ j' ∈ range (M2 + 1), pa i' * pb j' * (la i' * lb j') =\n      ((pa i * la i) / ∑ i' ∈ range (M1 + 1), pa i' * la i') *\n        ((pb j * lb j) / ∑ j' ∈ range (M2 + 1), pb j' * lb j') := by\n  have : ∑ i' ∈ range (M1 + 1), ∑ j' ∈ range (M2 + 1), pa i' * pb j' * (la i' * lb j') =\n      (∑ i' ∈ range (M1 + 1), pa i' * la i') * ∑ j' ∈ range (M2 + 1), pb j' * lb j' := by\n    rw [Finset.sum_mul_sum]\n    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i' _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun j' _ => ?_))\n    ring\n  rw [this]\n  field_simp\n\n/-! ### Total population -/\n\n/-- Law (support bound, pmf) of the total of a list of independent species counts. -/\nnoncomputable def totalLaw : List Sp → ℕ × (ℕ → ℝ)\n  | [] => (0, fun n => if n = 0 then 1 else 0)\n  | s :: ss => (s.M + (totalLaw ss).1, conv s.M (totalLaw ss).1 (spPost s) (totalLaw ss).2)\n\ntheorem totalLaw_spec : ∀ l : List Sp, (∀ s ∈ l, (SpValid s)) →\n    IsLaw (totalLaw l).1 (totalLaw l).2 ∧\n    mean (totalLaw l).1 (totalLaw l).2 = (l.map (fun s => mean s.M (spPost s))).sum ∧\n    var (totalLaw l).1 (totalLaw l).2 = (l.map (fun s => var s.M (spPost s))).sum\n  | [], _ => by\n    refine ⟨⟨fun n => ?_, ?_⟩, ?_, ?_⟩\n    · simp only [totalLaw]; split_ifs <;> norm_num\n    · simp [totalLaw]\n    · simp [totalLaw, mean, E]\n    · simp [totalLaw, var, E, mean]\n  | s :: ss, hv => by\n    have hs : (SpValid s) := hv s (List.mem_cons_self ..)\n    obtain ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩ := totalLaw_spec ss (fun t ht => hv t (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ ht))\n    have hl := post_isLaw hs\n    refine ⟨conv_isLaw hl h1, ?_, ?_⟩\n    · simp only [totalLaw, List.map_cons, List.sum_cons]\n      rw [mean_conv hl h1, h2]\n    · simp only [totalLaw, List.map_cons, List.sum_cons]\n      rw [var_conv hl h1, h3]\n\n/-- **Answer.** For independent species counts whose posteriors are defined by the Bayesian model\nabove: each species posterior is a probability law, its presence probability is given by the\nexplicit formula, a labelled camera encounter excludes absence when no false labels are possible,\nand the total population posterior is the convolution of the species laws, a probability law\nwhose mean and variance are the sums of the species means and variances. -/\ntheorem answer_theorem : ∀ l : List Sp, (∀ s ∈ l, (SpValid s)) →\n    (∀ s ∈ l, IsLaw s.M (spPost s) ∧\n      (spPresence s) = 1 - (1 - s.omega) * (spCamLik s) 0 s.y * (gridAvg s.gC) (pattern s.k s.nG) / (spZ s)) ∧\n    IsLaw (totalLaw l).1 (totalLaw l).2 ∧\n    mean (totalLaw l).1 (totalLaw l).2 = (l.map (fun s => mean s.M (spPost s))).sum ∧\n    var (totalLaw l).1 (totalLaw l).2 = (l.map (fun s => var s.M (spPost s))).sum := by\n  intro l hv\n  exact ⟨fun s hs => ⟨post_isLaw (hv s hs), presence_formula (hv s hs)⟩, totalLaw_spec l hv⟩\n\n/-! ### The lake: data and explicit modelling choices -/\n\n/-- Rescale the parameters of a grid by a factor `a` (used for transfer/coverage). -/\ndef scaledGrid (g : Grid) (a : ℝ) : Grid where\n  K := g.K\n  w := g.w\n  x := fun i => a * g.x i\n\ntheorem scaledGrid_pos {g : Grid} (hg : (GridPos g)) {a : ℝ} (h0 : 0 < a) (h1 : a ≤ 1) :\n    (GridPos (scaledGrid g a)) := by\n  refine ⟨hg.K_pos, hg.w_pos, fun i hi => ?_⟩\n  have := hg.x_in i hi\n  show 0 < a * g.x i ∧ a * g.x i < 1\n  constructor\n  · exact mul_pos h0 this.1\n  · nlinarith [this.1, this.2]\n\ntheorem scaledGrid_ok {g : Grid} (hg : (GridOk g)) {a : ℝ} (h0 : 0 ≤ a) (h1 : a ≤ 1) :\n    (GridOk (scaledGrid g a)) := by\n  refine ⟨hg.w_nonneg, hg.w_sum, fun i hi => ?_⟩\n  have := hg.x_mem i hi\n  show 0 ≤ a * g.x i ∧ a * g.x i ≤ 1\n  constructor\n  · exact mul_nonneg h0 this.1\n  · nlinarith [this.1, this.2]\n\n/-- Fraction of the mapped lake area (57 782.56 m²) covered by the 9 camera footprints (1260 m²)\nof one pass. -/\nnoncomputable def coverFrac : ℝ := 1260 / 57782.56\n\ntheorem coverFrac_bounds : 0 < coverFrac ∧ coverFrac < 1 := by\n  unfold coverFrac; constructor <;> norm_num\n\n/-- One panel species.  `om` prior presence probability; `y` camera labels; `calHits` correct\nlabels out of 160 reference encounters; `fpHits` false labels in 200 fish-free reference videos;\n`k` eDNA-positive grabs of 18; `tau` field/reference detectability transfer factor. -/\nnoncomputable def mkSp (om : ℝ) (y calHits fpHits k : ℕ) (tau : ℝ) : Sp where\n  M := 100000\n  omega := om\n  y := y\n  m := 36\n  c := 2\n  gF := calGrid 20 fpHits 200\n  gQ := scaledGrid (calGrid 20 calHits 160) (coverFrac * tau)\n  k := k\n  nG := 18\n  gC := calGrid 20 1 16\n  gT := flatGrid 20\n\n/-- The eight panel species, in order: perch, roach, ruffe, pike, burbot, bleak, vendace, bream. -/\nnoncomputable def lakeSpecies (tau : ℝ) : List Sp :=\n  [ mkSp (97 / 100) 39 97 2 17 tau, mkSp (9 / 10) 26 82 2 17 tau,\n    mkSp (8 / 10) 1 29 1 14 tau, mkSp (9 / 10) 1 67 6 9 tau,\n    mkSp (6 / 10) 1 24 4 1 tau, mkSp (35 / 100) 0 92 1 1 tau,\n    mkSp (3 / 10) 0 78 3 0 tau, mkSp (35 / 100) 1 75 2 1 tau ]\n\ntheorem mkSp_valid {om : ℝ} (h0 : 0 < om) (h1 : om < 1) {y : ℕ} (hy : y ≤ 200000)\n    (calHits fpHits : ℕ) {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ 18) {tau : ℝ} (t0 : 0 < tau) (t1 : tau ≤ 1) :\n    (SpValid (mkSp om y calHits fpHits k tau)) := by\n  have hc := coverFrac_bounds\n  have ha0 : 0 < coverFrac * tau := mul_pos hc.1 t0\n  have ha1 : coverFrac * tau ≤ 1 := by nlinarith [hc.2]\n  have k20 : 0 < 20 := by norm_num\n  have kk : 0 < 16 := by norm_num\n  have hM : 1 ≤ (100000 : ℕ) := by norm_num\n  have hy' : y ≤ 2 * 100000 := by omega\n  exact ⟨hM, h0, h1,\n    calGrid_pos 20 _ _ k20, scaledGrid_pos (calGrid_pos 20 _ _ k20) ha0 ha1,\n    calGrid_pos 20 _ _ k20, flatGrid_pos 20 k20,\n    calGrid_ok 20 _ _ k20, scaledGrid_ok (calGrid_ok 20 _ _ k20) ha0.le ha1,\n    calGrid_ok 20 _ _ k20, flatGrid_ok 20 k20,\n    hy', hk⟩\n\ntheorem lake_valid {tau : ℝ} (t0 : 0 < tau) (t1 : tau ≤ 1) : ∀ s ∈ lakeSpecies tau, (SpValid s) := by\n  intro s hs\n  simp only [lakeSpecies, List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil, or_false] at hs\n  rcases hs with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;>\n    exact mkSp_valid (by norm_num) (by norm_num) (by norm_num) _ _ (by norm_num) t0 t1\n\n/-- **Conclusion for the lake.**  For every field/reference detectability transfer c) (hU : m1 + c ≤ U) :\n    1 - (m2 - m1 ^ 2) / c ^ 2 ≤ ∑' n : ℕ, (if L < (n : ℝ) ∧ (n : ℝ) < U then w n else 0) := by\n  have hc2 : 0 < c ^ 2 := by positivity\n  -- tail bound: indicator(|n-m1| ≥ c) w ≤ (n-m1)^2 w / c^2\n  set u : ℕ → ℝ := fun n => ((n : ℝ) -     "command": "cd /work/v4; cat > gen.py <<'EOF'\nimport math, sys\nfrom fractions import Fraction as Fr\nsys.path.insert(0,'/work/v4')\nfrom data import Y, hits, area, foot, wilson, sp, hab, sz\nA={h:Fr(str(area[h])) for h in hab}\ndef rnd(x,up):\n    x=Fr(x).limit_denominator(10**9)\n    f=x*100\n    return Fr(math.ceil(f) if up else math.floor(f),100)\ncells={}\nfor s in sp:\n    L=[]\n    for h in hab:\n        for z in sz:\n            lo,hi=wilson(hits[(s,z)],80)\n            L.append(dict(y=Y[(s,h,z)],g=Fr(6*foot[h])/A[h],A=A[h],dlo=rnd(lo,False),dhi=rnd(hi,True)))\n    cells[s]=L\ndef lit(q):\n    q=Fr(q)\n    return f\"({q.numerator} / {q.denominator} : ℝ)\" if q.denominator!=1 else f\"({q.numerator} : ℝ)\"\ndef meanR(y,r): return (y+1)*r/(1-r)+y\ndef varR(y,r): return (y+1)*r/(1-r)**2\ndef rLo(c,th,kl): return (1-1/(1+kl*c['A']))*(1-c['g']*th*c['dhi'])\ndef rHi(c,tl,kh): return (1-1/(1+kh*c['A']))*(1-c['g']*tl*c['dlo'])\ndef box(cs,tl,th,kl,kh):\n    return (sum(meanR(c['y'],rLo(c,th,kl)) for c in cs), sum(meanR(c['y'],rHi(c,tl,kh)) for c in cs), sum(varR(c['y'],rHi(c,tl,kh)) for c in cs))\nscen=[('full',Fr(1,4),Fr(1),Fr(1,20),Fr(5)),('tau1',Fr(1),Fr(1),Fr(1,20),Fr(5)),('tauhalf',Fr(1,2),Fr(1,2),Fr(1,20),Fr(5)),('tauquarter',Fr(1,4),Fr(1,4),Fr(1,20),Fr(5))]\ngroups=[('perchC',cells['perch']),('roachC',cells['roach']),('ruffeC',cells['ruffe']),('pikeC',cells['pike']),('lakeC',sum(cells.values(),[]))]\nout={}\nfor name,tl,th,kl,kh in scen:\n    for g,cs in groups:\n        lo,hi,v=box(cs,tl,th,kl,kh)\n        Lb=Fr(math.floor(lo)); Ub=Fr(math.ceil(hi)); Vb=Fr(math.ceil(v))\n        c=Fr(math.ceil(math.sqrt(10*float(Vb))))\n        while c*c<10*Vb: c+=1\n        out[(name,g)]=dict(Lb=Lb,Ub=Ub,Vb=Vb,c=c,Lc=Lb-c,Uc=Ub+c,lo=float(lo),hi=float(hi),v=float(v))\nif __name__=='__main__':\n    for k,v in out.items(): print(k,{a:(round(b,1) if isinstance(b,float) else str(b)) for a,b in v.items()})\nEOF\npython3 gen.py"

    "command": "cd /work/v4; cat > gen2.py <<'EOF'\nimport sys\nsys.path.insert(0,'/work/v4')\nfrom gen import *\ndef cell_lit(c): return f\"⟨{c['y']}, {lit(c['g'])}, {lit(c['A'])}, {lit(c['dlo'])}, {lit(c['dhi'])}⟩\"\nnames={'perch':'perchC','roach':'roachC','ruffe':'ruffeC','pike':'pikeC'}\ns='''\n/-! ### The lake: data (SYNTHETIC survey VCS-LK-001) -/\n\n/-- Cells (habitat × size class) of one species, in the order littoral-small, littoral-large,\nopen-small, open-large, deep-small, deep-large.  `y` = camera labels summed over 3 stations × 2 passes;\n`g = 6·footprint/area` with footprints 120/180/120 m² and mapped areas 17310.23/29050.15/11422.18 m²;\n`[dlo,dhi]` = 95 % Wilson interval of the reference-video calibration hits/80, rounded outward to 0.01. -/\n'''\nfor sp_ in sp:\n    s+=f\"def {names[sp_]} : List Cell :=\\n  [ \"+\",\\n    \".join(cell_lit(c) for c in cells[sp_])+\" ]\\n\\n\"\ns+=\"def lakeC : List Cell := perchC ++ roachC ++ ruffeC ++ pikeC\\n\"\ns+='''\nopen Classical in\n/-- Posterior summary of the total count in the cells `cs`: the convolution law is a probability\nlaw with the stated moments; its mean lies in `[Lb,Ub]`; its variance is `≤ Vb`; it puts no mass below\nthe number of labelled encounters; and the interval `(Lc,Uc)` has probability `≥ 0.9`. -/\ndef Summary (cs : List Cell) (τ κ : ℝ) (d : Cell → ℝ) (Lb Ub Vb Lc Uc : ℝ) : Prop :=\n  Law (lawOf (cs.map (fitOf τ κ d))) (M1 (cs.map (fitOf τ κ d)))\n      (V (cs.map (fitOf τ κ d)) + M1 (cs.map (fitOf τ κ d)) ^ 2) ∧\n  Lb ≤ M1 (cs.map (fitOf τ κ d)) ∧ M1 (cs.map (fitOf τ κ d)) ≤ Ub ∧\n  V (cs.map (fitOf τ κ d)) ≤ Vb ∧\n  (∀ n : ℕ, n < (cs.map (fun c => c.y)).sum → lawOf (cs.map (fitOf τ κ d)) n = 0) ∧\n  9 / 10 ≤ ∑' n : ℕ, (if Lc < (n : ℝ) ∧ (n : ℝ) < Uc then lawOf (cs.map (fitOf τ κ d)) n else 0)\n\ntheorem summary_of_box {τl τh κl κh : ℝ} (hb : Box τl τh κl κh) {cs : List Cell}\n    (hok : ∀ c ∈ cs, CellOk c) {τ κ : ℝ} (hτ : τl ≤ τ ∧ τ ≤ τh) (hκ : κl ≤ κ ∧ κ ≤ κh)\n    {d : Cell → ℝ} (hd : ∀ c ∈ cs, c.dlo ≤ d c ∧ d c ≤ c.dhi)\n    {Lb Ub Vb Lc Uc c : ℝ} (h1 : Lb ≤ boxLo τh κl cs) (h2 : boxHi τl κh cs ≤ Ub)\n    (h3 : boxV τl κh cs ≤ Vb) (hc : 0 < c) (hc2 : 10 * Vb ≤ c ^ 2) (hL : Lc ≤ Lb - c)\n    (hU : Ub + c ≤ Uc) : Summary cs τ κ d Lb Ub Vb Lc Uc := by\n  obtain ⟨ok, lo, hi, vb, ys⟩ := list_box hb cs hok hτ hκ hd\n  have hl := lawOf_law _ ok\n  refine ⟨hl, by linarith, by linarith, by linarith, ?_, ?_⟩\n  · intro n hn\n    exact lawOf_below _ ok n (by rw [ys]; exact hn)\n  · have hch := cheb_interval hl hc (L := Lc) (U := Uc) (by linarith) (by linarith)\n    have e : V (cs.map (fitOf τ κ d)) + M1 (cs.map (fitOf τ κ d)) ^ 2 - M1 (cs.map (fitOf τ κ d)) ^ 2\n        = V (cs.map (fitOf τ κ d)) := by ring\n    rw [e] at hch\n    have hc2' : 0 < c ^ 2 := by positivity\n    have : V (cs.map (fitOf τ κ d)) / c ^ 2 ≤ 1 / 10 := by\n      rw [div_le_iff₀ hc2']; linarith\n    linarith\n\ntheorem lake_cells_ok : ∀ c ∈ lakeC, CellOk c := by\n  simp only [lakeC, perchC, roachC, ruffeC, pikeC, List.mem_append, List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil, or_false]\n  intro c hc\n  rcases hc with ((hc | hc) | hc) | hc <;>\n  rcases hc with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;> norm_num [CellOk]\n'''\ndef stmt(name,tl,th,kl,kh):\n    r=lambda g:out[(name,g)]\n    parts=[]\n    for g,_ in groups:\n        o=r(g)\n        parts.append(f\"Summary {g} τ κ d {lit(o['Lb'])} {lit(o['Ub'])} {lit(o['Vb'])} {lit(o['Lc'])} {lit(o['Uc'])}\")\n    return parts\nfor name,tl,th,kl,kh in scen:\n    parts=stmt(name,tl,th,kl,kh)\n    s+=f'''\ntheorem answer_{name} : ∀ (τ κ : ℝ) (d : Cell → ℝ), {lit(tl)} ≤ τ → τ ≤ {lit(th)} → {lit(kl)} ≤ κ → κ ≤ {lit(kh)} →\n    (∀ c ∈ lakeC, c.dlo ≤ d c ∧ d c ≤ c.dhi) →\n    {\" ∧\\n    \".join(parts)} := by\n  intro τ κ d t1 t2 k1 k2 hd\n  have hb : Box {lit(tl)} {lit(th)} {lit(kl)} {lit(kh)} := by\n    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> norm_num\n  have hok := lake_cells_ok\n'''\n    sub={'perchC':'(fun c hc => hok c (by simp [lakeC, hc]))','roachC':'(fun c hc => hok c (by simp [lakeC, hc]))','ruffeC':'(fun c hc => hok c (by simp [lakeC, hc]))','pikeC':'(fun c hc => hok c (by simp [lakeC, hc]))','lakeC':'hok'}\n    lines=[]\n    for g,_ in groups:\n        o=out[(name,g)]\n        hdarg = \"(fun c hc => hd c (by simp [lakeC, hc]))\" if g!='lakeC' else \"hd\"\n        lines.append(f\"summary_of_box hb {sub[g]} ⟨t1, t2⟩ ⟨k1, k2⟩ {hdarg} (c := {lit(o['c'])})\\n      (by norm_num [boxLo, rLo, meanR, {g}]) (by norm_num [boxHi, rHi, meanR, {g}])\\n      (by norm_num [boxV, rHi, varR, {g}]) (by norm_num) (by norm_num) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)\")\n    s+=\"  exact ⟨\"+\",\\n    \".join(lines)+\"⟩\\n\"\nopen('G.lean','w').write(s)\nEOF\npython3 gen2.py && cat A.lean B.lean C.lean D.lean E.lean F.lean G.lean > ALL.lean; export LEAN_PATH=$(ls -d /harness/.lake/packages/*/.lake/build/lib/lean | tr '\\n' ':'); time lean ALL.lean 2>&1 | grep -v \"^$\" | grep -B2 -A25 error | head -80"

PRESENCE (option (b) authorised by the reviewer): the four species perch, roach, ruffe and pike are\n   ASSUMED present (≥ 1 living individual); the count inference below is made for these four species only.\n   Presence of burbot, bleak, vendace, common bream and non-panel taxa is not assessed, and their fish are\n   NOT in any total.  `Summary` additionally proves that, if the camera labels are correct, the posterior\n   has no mass below the number of labels, so those four species are then certainly present.\n2. Cells = species × habitat (littoral/open/deep) × size bin (≤ 8 cm / > 8 cm); cell counts are a priori\n   independent.  Prior of a cell: `N ~ Geometric(ρ)` = Gamma(shape 1)–Poisson marginal with prior mean\n   `κ·A` fish (`κ` fish per m², `A` the mapped habitat area).  `κ` is not identifiable: we let it range over\n   [0.05, 5] fish/m² (≈ 5–500 fish per 100 m²; boreal-lake fish biomass of order 10–300 kg/ha spread\n   over fish of 5–50 g) and prove the conclusions for every value in that range.\n3. Observation: each fish of the cell is independently labelled by the cameras with probability\n   `p = g·τ·d`  (g = 6·footprint/area = fraction covered in 2 passes × 3 stations; d = reference-video\n   detection probability; τ = field/reference transfer factor).  `y ~ Binomial(N, p)`.  This treats the two\n   passes as one trial with probability 2×(per-pass) (accurate when p ≪ 1; here p ≤ 0.1), ignores\n   repeat encounters of the same fish, treats the mapped areas as exact and assumes fish are spread\n   uniformly inside a habitat/size cell.  Camera false labels are not modelled (≤ 4 % per fish-free\n   video; they would lower the means slightly, most for the y = 1 ruffe and pike cells).\n4. `d` is allowed to lie anywhere in the 95 % Wilson interval of its calibration (rounded outward), per cell;\n   `τ` is NOT identifiable: reported as scenarios τ = 1, 1/2, 1/4 and as the envelope τ ∈ [1/4, 1].\n   The results are therefore ENVELOPES over a parameter box, not a posterior over τ, d, κ.\n5. The total is the sum of independent cell counts (independence of cells given the parameters).\n\n## Proved (see theorems)\n* `cell_post_law`: from the geometric prior and binomial likelihood by Bayes' rule, the evidence is\n  explicit and the posterior of `N` is `y +` NegBin(y+1, r = (1-ρ)(1-p)), a probability law with\n  mean `(y+1)r/(1-r)+y` and variance `(y+1)r/(1-r)²` (normalisation and moment series proved).\n* `lawOf_law`: the total over independent cells is the convolution; its mean / variance are the sums.\n* `cheb_interval`: Chebyshev interval for a law with given moments.\n* `answer_full`, `answer_tau1`, `answer_tauhalf`, `answer_tauquarter`: for EVERY κ, τ and\n  detection `d` in the stated box, the species laws (perch, roach, ruffe, pike) and the total law are\n  probability laws whose means lie in the stated numeric intervals, whose variances are ≤ the stated bound,\n  with no mass below the number of labels and with ≥ 90 % probability in the stated interval.\n  (`Summary` spells out each of these claims.)\n-/\n\n'''\ns=s[:i]+hdr+s[i+len(\"open Finset\\n\"):]\nopen('/work/Model.lean','w').write(s)\nEOF\ncd /work; grep -c \"\" Model.lean; python3 - <<'EOF'\nimport sys\nsys.path.insert(0,'/work/v4')\nfrom gen import *\nfor k,v in out.items():\n    print(k, v['Lb'],v['Ub'],v['Vb'], round(v['Vb']**.5**1 if False else float(v['Vb'])**.5), v['Lc'],v['Uc'])\nEOF"

linarith\n\n/-- A scenario cell: `y` labels; the labelling probability lies in `[plo,phi]` and the prior ratio\nin `[qlo,qhi]`. -/\nstructure Cell where\n  y : ℕ\n  plo : ℝ\n  phi : ℝ\n  qlo : ℝ\n  qhi : ℝ\n\ndef CellOk (c : Cell) : Prop := 0 < c.plo ∧ c.plo ≤ c.phi ∧ c.phi < 1 ∧ 0 < c.qlo ∧ c.qlo ≤ c.qhi ∧ c.qhi < 1\n/-- `P c`, `Q c` are the (unknown) labelling probability and prior ratio of each cell. -/\ndef Within (cs : List Cell) (P Q : Cell → ℝ) : Prop :=\n  ∀ c ∈ cs, c.plo ≤ P c ∧ P c ≤ c.phi ∧ c.qlo ≤ Q c ∧ Q c ≤ c.qhi\n\ndef fits (cs : List Cell) (P Q : Cell → ℝ) : List Fit := cs.map (fun c => ⟨c.y, P c, Q c⟩)\nnoncomputable def rLo (c : Cell) : ℝ := (1 - c.qhi) * (1 - c.phi)\nnoncomputable def rHi (c : Cell) : ℝ := (1 - c.qlo) * (1 - c.plo)\n\n/-- Posterior summary of the total of the cells `cs` for every admissible `P`, `Q`: the total law is a\nprobability law (mean `M1`, variance `V`); exact hn)⟩\n  intro cs\n  induction cs with\n  | nil => intro _ P Q _; simp [fits, M1, V, Ysum]\n  | cons c cs ih =>\n    intro hok P Q hw\n    obtain ⟨i1, i2, i3, i4, i5⟩ := ih (fun x hx => hok x (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hx)) P Q\n      (fun x hx => hw x (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hx))\n    obtain ⟨hp0, hpp, hp1, hq0, hqq, hq1⟩ := hok c (List.mem_cons_self ..)\n    obtain ⟨w1, w2, w3, w4⟩ := hw c (List.mem_cons_self ..)\n    have g1 : 0 < 1 - P c := by linarith\n    have g2 : 0 < 1 - Q c := by linarith\n    have f1 : 0 ≤ rLo c := mul_nonneg (by linarith) (by linarith)\n    have f2 : rLo c ≤ (1 - Q c) * (1 - P c) := mul_le_mul (by linarith) (by linarith) g1.le g2.le\n    have f3 : (1 - Q c) * (1 - P c) ≤ rHi c := mul_le_mul (by linarith) (by linarith) g1.le (by linarith)\n    have f4 : rHi c < 1 := by unfold rHi; nlinarith [mul_pos (by linarith : 0 < 1 - c.qlo) (by linarith : 0 < 1 - c.plo)]\n    have m1 := meanR_mono c.y f1 f2 (by linarith)\n    have m2 := meanR_mono c.y (by positivity) f3 f4\n    have e : M1 (fits (c :: cs) P Q) = meanR c.y ((1 - Q c) * (1 - P c)) + M1 (fits cs P Q) := by\n      simp [fits, M1, rr]\n    have e' : V (fits (c :: cs) P Q) = varR c.y ((1 - Q c) * (1 - P c)) + V (fits cs P Q) := by\n      simp [fits, V, rr]\n    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩\n    · intro f hf\n      simp only [fits, List.map_cons, List.mem_cons] at hf\n      rcases hf with rfl | hf\n      · exact ⟨by linarith, by linarith, by linarith, by linarith⟩\n      · exact i1 f (by simpa [fits] using hf)\n    · simp only [List.map_cons, List.sum_cons]; \n    for gname,_ in groups:\n        o=out[(name,gname)]\n        parts.append(f\"Summary ({gname} {a}) {L(o['Lb'])} {L(o['Ub'])} {L(o['Vb'])}\" if gname!='lakeC' else f\"Summary (lakeC {a}) {L(o['Lb'])} {L(o['Ub'])} {L(o['Vb'])}\")\n    t=f\"theorem answer_{name} :\\n    \"+\" ∧\\n    \".join(parts)+\" := by\\n\"\n    t+=f\"  have hok : ∀ x ∈ lakeC {a}, CellOk x := by\\n    simp only [lakeC, perchC, roachC, ruffeC, pikeC, sp, mk, gL, AL, gO, AO, gD, AD, CellOk, List.forall_mem_append, List.forall_mem_cons, List.forall_mem_nil]\\n    norm_num\\n\"\n    sub=lambda gn: f\"(fun x hx => hok x (by simp [lakeC, hx]))\" if gn!='lakeC' else \"hok\"\n    t+=\"  refine ⟨\"+\", \".join(f\"summary_of_box _ {sub(gn)} ?_ ?_ ?_\" for gn,_ in groups)+\"⟩\\n\"\n    t+=f\"  all_goals simp only [boxdummy]\\n\"\n    return t\nopen('G0.lean','w').write(g)\nfor k in ['full','tau1']:\n    pass\nEOF\npython3 gen3.py;   "content": "import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecificLimits.Normed\nimport Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Ring.InfiniteSum\nimport Mathlib.Data.Nat.Choose.Basic\nimport Mathlib.Tactic.Positivity\nimport Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp\nimport Mathlib.Tactic.Ring\nimport Mathlib.Tactic.NormNum\nimport Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith\nimport Mathlib.Tactic.LinearCombination\n\nopen Finset\nstructure Law (w : ℕ → ℝ) (m1 m2 : ℝ) : Prop where\n  nonneg : ∀ n, 0 ≤ w n\n  total : HasSum w 1\n  first : HasSum (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) * w n) m1\n  second : HasSum (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ 2 * w n) m2\n\ndef cv (f g : ℕ → ℝ) (t : ℕ) : ℝ := ∑ kl ∈ antidiagonal t, f kl.1 * g kl.2\n\ndef delta0 (n : ℕ) : ℝ := if n = 0 then 1 else 0\n\ndef prior (ρ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ := ρ * (1 - ρ) ^ n\n\ndef lik (p : ℝ) (y n : ℕ) : ℝ := (n.choose y : ℝ) * p ^ y * (1 - p) ^ (n - y)\n\ndef unorm (y : ℕ) (p ρ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ := prior ρ n * lik p y n\n\nnoncomputable def post (y : ℕ) (p ρ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ := unorm y p ρ n / ∑' m, unorm y p ρ m\n\nnoncomputable def meanR (y : ℕ) (r : ℝ) : ℝ := ((y : ℝ) + 1) * r / (1 - r) + y\n\nnoncomputable def varR (y : ℕ) (r : ℝ) : ℝ := ((y : ℝ) + 1) * r / (1 - r) ^ 2\n\nstructure Fit where\n  y : ℕ\n  p : ℝ\n  ρ : ℝ\n\ndef rr (f : Fit) : ℝ := (1 - f.ρ) * (1 - f.p)\n\nnoncomputable def lawOf : List Fit → ℕ → ℝ\n  | [] => delta0\n  | f :: fs => cv (post f.y f.p f.ρ) (lawOf fs)\n\nnoncomputable def M1 (l : List Fit) : ℝ := (l.map (fun f => meanR f.y (rr f))).sum\n\nnoncomputable def V (l : List Fit) : ℝ := (l.map (fun f => varR f.y (rr f))).sum\n\n/-- A scenario cell: `y` labels; the labelling probability lies in `[plo,phi]` and the prior ratio\nin `[qlo,qhi]`. -/\nstructure Cell where\n  y : ℕ\n  plo : ℝ\n  phi : ℝ\n  qlo : ℝ\n  qhi : ℝ\n\n/-- `P c`, `Q c` are the (unknown) labelling probability and prior ratio of each cell. -/\ndef Within (cs : List Cell) (P Q : Cell → ℝ) : Prop :=\n  ∀ c ∈ cs, c.plo ≤ P c ∧ P c ≤ c.phi ∧ c.qlo ≤ Q c ∧ Q c ≤ c.qhi\n\ndef fits (cs : List Cell) (P Q : Cell → ℝ) : List Fit := cs.map (fun c => ⟨c.y, P c, Q c⟩)\n\n/-- Posterior summary of the total of the cells `cs` for every admissible `P`, `Q`: the total law is a\nprobability law (mean `M1`, variance `V`); `M1 ∈ [Lb,Ub]`, `V ≤ Vb`; no mass below the label count. -/\ndef Summary (cs : List Cell) (Lb Ub Vb : ℝ) : Prop := ∀ P Q : Cell → ℝ, Within cs P Q →\n  Law (lawOf (fits cs P Q)) (M1 (fits cs P Q)) (V (fits cs P Q) + M1 (fits cs P Q) ^ 2) ∧\n  Lb ≤ M1 (fits cs P Q) ∧ M1 (fits cs P Q) ≤ Ub ∧ V (fits cs P Q) ≤ Vb ∧\n  ∀ n : ℕ, n < (cs.map (fun c => c.y)).sum → lawOf (fits cs P Q) n = 0\n\nfile /work/checks/e8c1bbd4cdd7432ca35690573741673c/submitted.lean\nlean_exit 0\nok False\ncompiles_alone True\nidentity_method kernel-expression-repr-v1\ndependency_faithful {'Summary': True, 'Cell': True, 'Cell.mk': True, 'Within': True, 'Cell.plo': True, 'Cell.phi': True, 'Cell.qlo': True, 'Cell.qhi': True, 'Law': True, 'Law.mk': True, 'lawOf': True, 'Fit': True, 'Fit.mk': True, 'lawOf._f': True, 'lawOf.match_1': True, 'delta0': True, 'cv': True, 'post': True, 'unorm'\ndependency_identities {'Summary': {'original_sha256': '7ae49fa1a0fc38d852eb484aac7edb5b51ca35d485820a9c190ec67b7d77d4cb', 'extracted_sha256': '7ae49fa1a0fc38d852eb484aac7edb5b51ca35d485820a9c190ec67b7d77d4cb'}, 'Cell': {'original_sha256': 'a5b666fe1877af15640dd2125a21c3d7ae5b888f8c4353dc36a031ddc2fc0ece', 'extracted_sha2\nunranged []\nadded_assumptions []\nconclusions_as_proved {'cell_posterior': '∀ (y : ℕ) (p ρ : ℝ), 0 < p → p < 1 → 0 < ρ → ρ < 1 → Law (post y p ρ) (meanR y ((1 - ρ) * (1 - p))) (varR y ((1 - ρ) * (1 - p)) + meanR y ((1 - ρ) * (1 - p)) ^ 2)', 'answer_full': 'Summary (perchC (1 / 4) 1 (1 / 20) 5) 1431 8941 2247795 ∧ Summary (roachC (1 / 4) 1 (1 / 20) 5) 120\nextracted_file /work/checks/e8c1bbd4cdd7432ca35690573741673c/extracted.lean\nerrors []",

This cycle's candidate is checkable and passed the harness check; it's ready for your review. The verdict is "proved", the extraction is faithful for all five conclusions, and there are no added axioms and no `sorry`. The check directory is `checks/9cc91935bee0423ca52fb92fc623db74`.

**What changed**
- **Lean-proved numbers.** I replaced the grid and 1/n prior with a conjugate model, so every reported population number is now a Lean theorem. Python only proposed the bounds; Lean checks them with exact rational arithmetic and monotonicity.
- **Presence.** I used your option (b). Perch, roach, ruffe and pike are assumed present with probability 1, and only those four are estimated. The omega table is gone. Burbot, bleak, vendace, bream and non-panel fish are not assessed and are not in any total.
- **File size.** The check tool caps the Lean body at 24,000 bytes, so I rebuilt the file compactly. This dropped the Chebyshev interval from the previous draft. The result is claimed as mean ranges and variance bounds only, not population intervals.

**Model** (all choices are exposed in the Lean header and `report.txt`)
- There are 24 independent cells (species × habitat × size bin).
- The prior is N ~ Geometric(ρ), with prior mean κ·A fish and κ in [0.05, 5] fish/m². This κ range is not identifiable from the data.
- Each fish is labelled by the cameras with probability p = (6·footprint/area)·τ·d.
  - d is the reference-video detection, taken from an outward-rounded 95% Wilson interval of hits/80.
  - τ is the field/reference transfer factor, which these data cannot identify.
- eDNA and sonar are not used for abundance.

**Proved in Lean**
- Bayes' rule gives the cell posterior as y plus a negative binomial, with explicit mean (y+1)r/(1−r)+y and variance (y+1)r/(1−r)².
- The total is the convolution of the cell laws, and its mean and variance add.
- No posterior mass lies below the camera label count.
- Posterior mean ranges and variance bounds, for every p and ρ in the stated box:

| Case | Perch | Roach | Ruffe | Pike | Total, four species |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| τ = 1 | 1431–2236 | 1205–2101 | 605–2253 | 317–663 | 3560–7251 |
| τ = 1/2 | 2767–4474 | 2313–4204 | 1113–4493 | 611–1330 | 6806–14499 |
| τ = 1/4 | 5176–8941 | 4273–8400 | 1914–8922 | 1126–2659 | 12491–28920 |
| τ ∈ [1/4, 1] | 1431–8941 | 1205–8400 | 605–8922 | 317–2659 | 3560–28920 |

**For your review**
- The ranges are envelopes over a parameter box, not posterior probabilities for τ, d or κ. The spread across τ (about a factor of 4) dominates the uncertainty.
- Presence is assumed. Pike and ruffe rest on a single camera label each, and camera false labels are not modelled.
- Two passes are pooled into one binomial, re-detections are ignored, mapped areas are treated as exact, and fish are assumed uniform within a cell.
- Cells with no labels get posterior mass from the geometric prior, so the ruffe and pike totals are largely prior- and detectability-driven.
- The total is a lower-type estimate of the lake population: other species and unmapped habitat are excluded.

In the Lean statements, `Summary (perchC a b c d)` takes natural-number arguments meaning τ ∈ [a/4, b/4] and κ ∈ [c/20, d/20]. This encoding only lets the harness match the statements exactly; it has no scientific meaning. I have not self-approved anything; the decision is yours.

The model was changed to a conjugate family with a closed-form posterior, so the\n   posterior mean and variance bounds of every species and of the total are Lean theorems (answer_full, answer_tau1, answer_tauhalf,\n   answer_tauquarter). Python (v4/gen.py) only proposed the rounded bounds; Lean checks them with exact rational arithmetic and monotonicity.\n2. Presence: option (b). Perch, roach, ruffe and pike are ASSUMED present (probability 1); the inference is conditional on that and covers these\n   four species only. The omega table is gone. Burbot, bleak, vendace, common bream and non-panel fish are not assessed and are not in any total.\n   Lean also proves that, if the camera labels are correct, the posterior has no mass below the label count (so these species are then certainly present).\n3. Kept from cycle 3: normalised laws, total = convolution of independent cell laws with additive mean/variance (now for infinite-support laws), camera evidence\n   excludes N=0. Dropped: grid discretisation, 1/n prior, Chebyshev interval (the 24 kB source limit forced a smaller file).\n\nMODEL (choices; not inferred)\n cell = species x habitat (littoral/open/deep) x size bin (24 cells), independent. Prior N ~ Geometric(rho) (= Gamma(1)-Poisson marginal) with prior mean kappa*A\n (A = mapped area), kappa in [0.05,5] fish/m2 (unidentified; rough range from boreal-lake fish biomass 10-300 kg/ha and 5-50 g fish).\n y ~ Binomial(N,p), p = (6*footprint/area)*tau*d: 3 stations x 2 passes pooled into one binomial with doubled probability, d = reference-video detection\n (95% Wilson interval of hits/80, rounded outward), tau = field/reference transfer (UNIDENTIFIABLE).\n Proved: posterior of N = y + NegBin(y+1, r=(1-rho)(1-p)), mean (y+1)r/(1-r)+y, variance (y+1)r/(1-r)^2 (cell_posterior); total law = convolution (lawOf_law).\n eDNA and sonar are not used for abundance (eDNA read fractions are not abundances; sonar has no species identity and 38-58% false-positive rate).\n\nPROVED RESULTS: posterior mean range, variance bound, sd bound. Hold for EVERY labelling probability and prior ratio in the box (kappa in [0.05,5], d in its interval, tau as stated).\n envelope tau in [1/4,1]: perch 1431-8941 (var<=2247795, sd<=1499); roach 1205-8400 (var<=2593063, sd<=1610); ruffe 605-8922 (var<=14916093, sd<=3862); pike 317-2659 (var<=1233022, sd<=1110); TOTAL (4 species) 3560-28920 (var<=20989972, sd<=4581)\n tau = 1: perch 1431-2236 (var<=139497, sd<=373); roach 1205-2101 (var<=161420, sd<=402); ruffe 605-2253 (var<=954125, sd<=977); pike 317-663 (var<=77094, sd<=278); TOTAL (4 species) 3560-7251 (var<=1332135, sd<=1154)\n tau = 1/2: perch 2767-4474 (var<=561548, sd<=749); roach 2313-4204 (var<=648647, sd<=805); ruffe 1113-4493 (var<=3789187, sd<=1947); pike 611-1330 (var<=309003, sd<=556); TOTAL (4 species) 6806-14499 (var<=5308383, sd<=2304)\n tau = 1/4: perch 5176-8941 (var<=2247795, sd<=1499); roach 4273-8400 (var<=2593063, sd<=1610); ruffe 1914-8922 (var<=14916093, sd<=3862); pike 1126-2659 (var<=1233022, sd<=1110); TOTAL (4 species) 12491-28920 (var<=20989972, sd<=4581)\n The ranges are ENVELOPES over a parameter box, not posterior probability statements about tau, d, kappa. tau cannot be learned from these data (paired field/reference test needed);\n it dominates the uncertainty (factor ~4 across tau in [1/4,1]).\n\nLIMITATIONS / FOR REVIEW\n - Cells with y=0 get posterior mass from the geometric prior (roughly 1/p), so ruffe and pike totals are largely prior/detectability driven.\n - Pike (1 label, ~3% false labels, eDNA 9/18 grabs) and ruffe (1 label): labels could be false; false labels are not modelled; presence is assumed by option (b).\n - Two passes pooled, re-detections of the same fish ignored, mapped areas exact (about 3% sd), uniform spread inside a cell, cells independent.\n - Quantity: living fish of these four species in the mapped strata in the late-August window; a LOWER-type estimate of the lake total (other species, unmapped habitat excluded).\n - No numbers other than those listed above are claimed as proved; cycle-3 Python numbers are superseded.\n\nCHECK RESULT (harness tool, this cycle): verdict \"proved\", extraction faithful for all five conclusions, no added axioms, no sorry (check dir checks/9cc91935bee0423ca52fb92fc623db74).\nReading the Lean statements: Summary (perchC a b c d) Lb Ub Vb with natural-number arguments means tau in [a/4, b/4], kappa in [c/20, d/20] fish/m2:\n answer_full (1 4 1 100): tau in [1/4,1]; answer_tau1 (4 4 1 100); answer_tauhalf (2 2 1 100); answer_tauquarter (1 1 1 100); kappa in [1/20,5] throughout.\n Summary says: for every labelling probability p and prior ratio rho of each cell inside the box, the total law is a probability law, mean in [Lb,Ub], variance <= Vb, no mass below the label count.\n (The natural-number encoding is only so the harness can match the statement exactly; it has no scientific meaning.)\n"
